## Batch 064 — 20 files scanned

### [HIGH] security theater

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/admin/security/route.ts`
- **Line:** 234
- **Instance:** suspend-user only flips `profiles.account_status` and the comment claims "auth middleware checks account_status on every request", but no apps/web middleware or auth path reads that column (`proxy.ts` and `lib/api-auth.ts` contain no account_status/suspend/banned check; the only apps/web references are this file and sso-check).
- **Risk:** A "suspended" user keeps full access via their live Clerk session because nothing enforces the suspension.
- **Fix:** Enforce account_status in the shared auth path (e.g. `getClerkAuthUser`/proxy) or revoke Clerk sessions on suspension, then update the comment to match reality.

### [MEDIUM] fail-open behavior

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/admin/security/route.ts`
- **Line:** 286
- **Instance:** When `clerk.users.banUser` fails, the handler logs "relying on middleware check" and still returns success, but that middleware check does not exist in apps/web.
- **Risk:** A failed Clerk ban silently leaves the banned user with full access while the admin sees a success response.
- **Fix:** Return an error (or at least a degraded-success status) when the Clerk ban fails until a real account_status enforcement layer exists.

### [MEDIUM] validation bypass

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/admin/security/route.ts`
- **Line:** 130
- **Instance:** The `eventType` query param is passed to `SecurityMonitoringService.getRecentEvents` via a bare `as Parameters<...>` cast with no allowlist validation, unlike `severity` which is validated at lines 113-116.
- **Risk:** Arbitrary client strings reach the service layer typed as a trusted enum, breaking the invariant the type promises and risking unexpected query behavior.
- **Fix:** Validate `eventType` against the known event-type enum before the call, mirroring the severity validation.

### [MEDIUM] request validation gap

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/admin/security/route.ts`
- **Line:** 125
- **Instance:** `parseInt(searchParams.get('limit') || '100', 10)` yields NaN for non-numeric input and `Math.min(NaN, 500)` propagates NaN into the service call (same pattern for `hours`/`limit` at lines 145-146).
- **Risk:** NaN limits reach the query layer, producing malformed SQL limits or unbounded result sets depending on the adapter.
- **Fix:** Validate the parsed integers with `Number.isFinite` and fall back to the documented defaults.

### [MEDIUM] request validation gap

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/admin/security/route.ts`
- **Line:** 191
- **Instance:** The 8KB body-size guard trusts the client-supplied Content-Length header (`parseInt(... ?? '0')`), so a chunked request without the header (or a lying header) bypasses the cap entirely.
- **Risk:** The memory-exhaustion guard the comment promises is bypassable, allowing oversized JSON bodies into `request.json()`.
- **Fix:** Enforce the cap on the actual body (read with a size-limited reader) instead of the advisory header.

### [HIGH] schema drift

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/admin/sso/route.ts`
- **Line:** 221
- **Instance:** The route inserts into `sso_connections` (columns provider_type, display_name, attribute_mapping, created_by, metadata_xml), but no migration anywhere in the repo (including canonical `apps/web/db/neon/`) creates an `sso_connections` table — grep over all `*.sql` finds no DDL.
- **Risk:** Every SSO create/list/delete call fails at runtime with relation-does-not-exist; the entire admin SSO feature is dead against the canonical schema.
- **Fix:** Add the `sso_connections` migration to `apps/web/db/neon/` (or remove/flag the route as not-yet-shipped) so code and schema agree.

### [HIGH] contract drift

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/admin/sso/route.ts`
- **Line:** 305
- **Instance:** DELETE selects column `provider` while POST inserts `provider_type` (line 221) and GET selects `provider_type` (line 112), and `SSOConnectionRow` (`apps/web/lib/server/neon-types.ts:349`) declares `provider` without display_name/attribute_mapping/created_by — the route's three handlers and the shared row type disagree on the column set.
- **Risk:** At most one of the three handlers can match the real schema; the others throw column-does-not-exist at runtime and the row type silently mistypes results.
- **Fix:** Pick one canonical column set in the migration, align all three queries and `SSOConnectionRow` to it.

### [MEDIUM] partial implementation

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/admin/sso/route.ts`

- **Instance:** `metadata_xml` (up to 500KB) and `attribute_mapping` are accepted and stored, but no code anywhere in the repo reads them back — there is no SAML/OIDC login flow consuming `sso_connections` metadata (only `auth/sso-check` touches the table).

- **Risk:** Users believe delegation responses were recorded when nothing was persisted, silently breaking the agent-delegation workflow.
- **Fix:** Create the `agent_delegations` migration and return a 5xx (or 501) instead of fake success when the schema is missing.

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/agents/communication/[id]/route.ts`

- **Risk:** Completed delegation decisions can be silently overwritten, producing lost updates and inconsistent downstream agent behavior.
- **Fix:** Add `and status = 'pending'` to the WHERE clause and return 409 when the delegation was already resolved.

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/agents/communication/route.ts`

- **Instance:** POST inserts into `agent_messages` but no migration in canonical `apps/web/db/neon/` (or anywhere in the repo) creates `agent_messages` or `agent_delegations` — grep over all `*.sql` finds no DDL.

### [HIGH] hardcoded success

### [LOW] semantic incorrectness

- **Fix:** Insert with status `'pending'`/`'sent'` and update to `'delivered'` when the recipient fetches it.

- **Risk:** Users are billed amounts decoupled from actual token usage — systematic over- or under-charging on every agent execution.
- **Fix:** Parse provider usage events from the stream and deduct the real token cost, reconciling against the estimate.

### [MEDIUM] async race

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/agents/execute/route.ts`
- **Line:** 200
- **Instance:** Pre-flight `CreditService.checkAvailable` and post-stream `deductCredits` are not an atomic reservation, so concurrent requests can all pass the balance check and overdraw; the idempotency key is even labeled 'reservation' though none is created.
- **Risk:** A user with minimal credits can run many parallel executions, driving the balance negative (cost leak on managed compute).
- **Fix:** Create an actual credit reservation/hold at pre-flight and settle it at flush, or deduct optimistically up-front and refund.

### [MEDIUM] silent failure

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/agents/execute/route.ts`
- **Line:** 242
- **Instance:** Credit deduction runs only in the TransformStream `flush()` callback, which never fires when the client disconnects mid-stream or the provider stream errors, and deduction failures are logged-and-ignored (lines 266-288).
- **Risk:** Aborted or erroring streams consume provider tokens that are never billed, an unmetered-cost leak.
- **Fix:** Bill via reservation at request start (settle/refund on completion) instead of relying solely on stream flush.

### [MEDIUM] SSRF

# Batch 065 — 20 files scanned

### [MEDIUM] idempotency gap

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/bulk/route.ts`
- **Line:** 79-131
- **Instance:** Up to 200 messages are inserted in a sequential loop with no transaction; a mid-loop failure leaves a partial batch persisted while the client receives a 500, and retrying duplicates every message that was sent without an explicit `id` (the documented "idempotent" contract at line 6 only holds for id-bearing messages).
- **Risk:** Client retries after transient DB errors produce duplicated chat messages and torn conversation state.
- **Fix:** Wrap the batch in a single transaction (or one multi-row insert) so the save is all-or-nothing.

### [HIGH] API contract violation

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/chat/folders/route.ts`
- **Line:** 115
- **Instance:** The route calls `select move_session_to_folder($1, $2)` with two arguments, but the only definition (`apps/web/db/neon/0022_chat_features.sql:53`) is `move_session_to_folder(p_session_id uuid, p_folder_id uuid, p_user_id text)` with no defaults, so Postgres raises "function move_session_to_folder(uuid, uuid) does not exist" on every call.
- **Risk:** The move-session-to-folder feature 500s on every invocation in production; additionally the omitted third argument is the user-ownership parameter, so any "fix" that adds a 2-arg overload without it would become an IDOR.
- **Fix:** Pass `userId` as the third argument: `select move_session_to_folder($1, $2, $3)` with `[sessionId, folderId, userId]`.

### [HIGH] schema drift

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/chat/folders/route.ts`
- **Line:** 88
- **Instance:** POST inserts into `chat_folders (user_id, name, color, icon, description, parent_folder_id, sort_order)` but the canonical migration (`apps/web/db/neon/0022_chat_features.sql:40-48`) creates `chat_folders` with only `id, user_id, name, color, sort_order, created_at, updated_at` — `icon`, `description`, and `parent_folder_id` do not exist in any migration, so folder creation fails with "column does not exist".
- **Risk:** Every folder create (and any PUT supplying icon/description/parentFolderId, lines 147-157, plus the `FolderRow` type at lines 41-52) fails at runtime; the folders feature is dead against the canonical schema.
- **Fix:** Add a migration creating the missing columns (with `parent_folder_id` self-FK) or strip the nonexistent columns from the route and schemas.

### [MEDIUM] ownership-check gap

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/chat/folders/route.ts`
- **Line:** 155-157
- **Instance:** `parentFolderId` (create at line 91, update at line 156) is persisted without verifying the parent folder belongs to the requesting user, so a folder can be parented under another user's folder id.
- **Risk:** Cross-tenant folder references corrupt hierarchy queries and can leak existence of other users' folder ids.
- **Fix:** Resolve `parentFolderId` with `where id = $1 and user_id = $2` before writing it (after the column actually exists, per the schema-drift finding).

### [LOW] malformed-response handling

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/chat/folders/route.ts`
- **Line:** 81
- **Instance:** `await request.json()` in POST/PUT/DELETE (lines 81, 107, 182) is not wrapped in try/catch, unlike the sibling chat routes, so malformed JSON throws a SyntaxError that surfaces as a 500 instead of a 400 validation error.
- **Risk:** Bad client payloads register as server errors, polluting error budgets/alerts and giving clients the wrong status semantics.
- **Fix:** Wrap `request.json()` in try/catch and throw `createError.validation('Invalid JSON in request body')` as the other chat routes do.

### [MEDIUM] ownership-check gap

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/route.ts`
- **Line:** 126
- **Instance:** PUT writes a client-supplied `projectId` (`project_id = case when $5::boolean then $6::text else project_id end`) without verifying the project exists or belongs to the requesting user (schema only bounds it to 200 chars).
- **Risk:** Conversations can be attached to other users' project ids or to garbage ids, corrupting project groupings and leaking valid project-id existence via behavior differences.
- **Fix:** Resolve the project with `where id = $1 and user_id = $2` (404 on miss) before persisting `project_id`.

### [LOW] pagination bug

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/route.ts`

- **Instance:** Message pagination orders by `created_at asc` with no tiebreaker column, so messages sharing a timestamp (e.g. bulk saves) have nondeterministic order across pages and can be skipped/duplicated between offset windows.
- **Risk:** Paginated history can render messages out of order or drop/duplicate rows at page boundaries.
- **Fix:** Order by `created_at asc, id asc` to make pagination deterministic.

### [MEDIUM] ownership-check gap

### [LOW] hardcoded success

- **Instance:** DELETE returns `{ success: true }` without checking affected row count, so deleting a nonexistent or other user's conversation id reports success instead of 404 (PATCH/DELETE message routes in the same family return 404 in this case).
- **Risk:** Clients cannot distinguish a real soft-delete from a no-op, masking sync bugs between client cache and server state.
- **Fix:** Check the affected count from `db.execute` and throw `createError.notFound` when zero rows matched.

### [HIGH] ownership-check gap

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/chat/reactions/route.ts`
- **Line:** 49-65
- **Instance:** POST toggles a reaction on any client-supplied `messageId` with no check that the message belongs to a conversation the caller owns (web_messages FK exists but no user scoping), and GET (lines 97-109) aggregates reactions for arbitrary `messageIds` with no ownership filter.
- **Risk:** Any authenticated user can attach reactions to, and read reaction state of, messages in other users' private conversations — a tenant-isolation failure on the web chat surface.
- **Fix:** Join `web_messages -> web_conversations` and require `web_conversations.user_id = $userId` in both the toggle and the aggregate queries.

### [MEDIUM] excessive data exposure

- **Fix:** Drop `user_ids` from the response and return only `count` plus the caller's own `userReacted` boolean.

### [MEDIUM] fail-open behavior

### [MEDIUM] idempotency gap

### [LOW] device-authorization reset

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/device/link/route.ts`
- **Line:** 91-107
- **Instance:** `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (device_id) DO UPDATE` unconditionally resets any existing row for a client-supplied `device_id` back to `pending` (clearing `user_id`, tokens, and prior status), and the link is not bound to the authenticated caller (`user_id` stays NULL, line 136).

## Batch 066 — 20 files scanned

### [HIGH] authorization gap / IDOR

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/github/install/route.ts`
- **Line:** 20
- **Instance:** `installation_id` is taken verbatim from the callback query string and is never verified against GitHub (no `GET /app/installations/{id}` ownership check); only a self-issued `state` cookie gates the request.
- **Risk:** An authenticated attacker who obtains a valid `state` cookie (from starting their own install flow) can replay the callback with a victim's enumerable numeric `installation_id`, and the upsert at line 49 (`on conflict (installation_id) do update set user_id = excluded.user_id`) reassigns the victim's GitHub App installation to the attacker — a cross-tenant ownership takeover that lets the attacker toggle PR review, choose the review model, and disconnect the victim.
- **Fix:** After receiving `installation_id`, call GitHub's installations API with the app JWT to confirm the authenticated user actually owns/administers that installation before inserting, and reject (don't reassign) on conflict where `user_id` differs.

### [MEDIUM] stale state / platform mismatch

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts`
- **Line:** 470
- **Instance:** Video task ownership is recorded only in process-local memory via `storeVideoTask(taskId, userId)`; the status route (`media/video/status/route.ts` line 311) fails closed with 403 when the lookup misses.
- **Risk:** On the serverless deployment target (the route declares `runtime = 'nodejs'`/`maxDuration` for Vercel), the generate and poll calls frequently land on different instances, so credits are reserved/charged at task creation but the user can never retrieve the finished video (status always 403) — an intermittent charge-without-deliverable bug.
- **Fix:** Persist task→owner mapping in durable shared storage (Redis or Neon) as the in-code comment already notes, instead of in-process memory.

- **Risk:** Requested portrait/resolution intent is silently dropped; all Runway videos render 16:9 regardless of the caller's `resolution` field.

### [MEDIUM] request validation gap

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/memory/[id]/route.ts`

- **Instance:** The `id` route param is passed straight into a uuid-typed SQL predicate (lines 29-35, 80-86, 117-122) with no UUID format validation; `user_memories.id` is `uuid` (db/neon/0010_memory.sql:2), so a non-UUID id makes Postgres throw a cast error that surfaces as a 500 instead of a 400/404.

- **Fix:** Validate `id` against a UUID regex (or zod `z.string().uuid()`) before querying and return `createError.validation`/`notFound` on mismatch.

- **Instance:** `body.category` is inserted with only an optional `trim()` — unlike `content` (capped at 10,000 chars, lines 81-83), `category` has no length cap or allowlist.

### [LOW] resource exhaustion

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/memory/sync/route.ts`

### [HIGH] cross-tenant leak
- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/search/route.ts`
- **Line:** 107-114
- **Instance:** The `type=popular` branch calls `get_popular_searches($1,$2)` which (per `apps/web/db/neon/0020_functions.sql:983-1002`) aggregates `query` text across ALL users with no per-user scoping and no minimum-count threshold, so any authenticated user receives the verbatim search-query strings typed by other users.
- **Risk:** Search queries frequently contain PII/sensitive terms; this exposes other tenants' private query text to any logged-in account, a serious privacy breach for a privacy-first product.
- **Fix:** Either scope popular-search aggregation per-user, or only surface queries above a high anonymity threshold (e.g. HAVING count >= N) with the raw text stripped/normalized.

### [HIGH] privilege escalation
- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/settings/team/route.ts`
- **Line:** 126-196
- **Instance:** `handleInvite` only checks that the requester is `owner` or `admin`, then inserts the new member with the caller-supplied `role` (including `owner`) without the "only owners may assign owner" guard that the sibling PATCH route enforces at `team/[memberId]/route.ts:139`.
- **Risk:** A non-owner admin can mint an `owner`-level membership (for an account they control), escalating beyond their privilege level and bypassing owner-only protections.
- **Fix:** Reject `role === 'owner'` in the invite path unless `requesterMembership.role === 'owner'`, mirroring the PATCH guard.

### [MEDIUM] approval-gate gap
- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/settings/2fa/setup/route.ts`
- **Line:** 56-68
- **Instance:** The setup upsert unconditionally sets `enabled = false, enabled_at = null` for an existing enrollment and replaces the TOTP secret, requiring only a valid session + CSRF (no current TOTP/step-up), while the DELETE route at `2fa/route.ts:92-114` requires a valid code to disable.
- **Risk:** A session-hijacker can effectively disable a victim's already-active 2FA by re-invoking setup, sidestepping the step-up verification that protects the disable flow.
- **Fix:** Require a valid current TOTP/backup code before overwriting an enrollment that is already `enabled`, or refuse to reset `enabled` for active rows.

### [MEDIUM] validation bypass
- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/settings/2fa/validate/route.ts`
- **Line:** 66-92
- **Instance:** TOTP verification accepts any code within the current/±1 time window (`user-preferences.ts:415-440`) but never records the consumed time-step/code, so a captured valid code can be replayed across `validate`, `verify`, and `disable` within its ~90s validity window.
- **Risk:** An attacker who observes one valid OTP (shoulder-surf, MITM, logs) can replay it for step-up auth or to disable 2FA, defeating the single-use intent of TOTP.
- **Fix:** Persist the last-accepted time-step (or last code hash) per user and reject codes whose step has already been consumed.

## Batch 069 — 20 files scanned

### [HIGH] swallowed exception

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/stripe-webhook/lib/handlers.ts`
- **Line:** 50 (same pattern at 122, 139, 182, 242, 260, 288, 310, 360)
- **Instance:** Every DB write inside `dispatchStripeEvent` attaches a `.catch()` that only logs and never rethrows, so the route's caller (`route.ts:91`) marks the Stripe event succeeded even when the subscription/credit update actually failed.
- **Risk:** Stripe receives 200 and never retries, and the idempotency table permanently blocks reprocessing, so a transient DB failure leaves subscription status/credits permanently wrong (e.g., user stays `active` after payment failure or keeps credits after cancellation).
- **Fix:** Rethrow (or return a failure result) from handler DB errors so the route returns 500 and `markEventFailed` allows Stripe's retry to reprocess the event.

### [HIGH] version skew

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/stripe-webhook/lib/handlers.ts`
- **Line:** 83 (also 224)
- **Instance:** `invoice.subscription` is accessed via `(invoice as unknown as { subscription?: string | null }).subscription` because the SDK typed `Invoice` for the pinned API version `2026-04-22.dahlia` (stripe-config.ts:8) no longer exposes a top-level `subscription` field (moved under the invoice parent in post-2025 Stripe API versions).
- **Risk:** On webhook endpoints configured to a current API version the field is absent at runtime, so `invoice.paid`/`invoice.payment_failed` silently skip the subscription-specific update and fall into the customer-wide fallback path with wrong data.
- **Fix:** Resolve the subscription id from the current API shape (invoice parent/subscription details) instead of casting around the SDK types, and add a test against a fixture rendered at the pinned API version.

### [HIGH] null handling bug

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/stripe-webhook/lib/handlers.ts`
- **Line:** 128-137
- **Instance:** The `invoice.paid` fallback (no resolvable subscription id) executes `update subscriptions set ... current_period_start = $2, current_period_end = $3 where stripe_customer_id = $4` with both period params resolved to `null` (lines 117-118 / 134-135).
- **Risk:** A successful payment whose subscription id cannot be resolved wipes the existing `current_period_start/current_period_end` for all of that customer's subscription rows, corrupting period-based credit allocation and entitlement checks.
- **Fix:** Use `coalesce` in SQL (or omit the period columns from the update) when period values are unknown so existing period data is preserved.

### [MEDIUM] async race

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/stripe-webhook/lib/handlers.ts`
- **Line:** 192-199 (same pattern at 368-375)
- **Instance:** Credit revocation reads the balance with `CreditService.getBalance` and then deducts that read amount with `CreditService.deductCredits` as two separate non-atomic operations.
- **Risk:** A concurrent user-initiated deduction between the read and the write makes the revocation amount stale, leaving residual credits after cancellation/dispute or failing the deduction outright.
- **Fix:** Perform revocation atomically in a single SQL/RPC (e.g., a `revoke_all_credits(user_id)` function) instead of read-then-write from the webhook.

### [MEDIUM] intent mismatch

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/stripe-webhook/lib/handlers.ts`
- **Line:** 193-199
- **Instance:** On `customer.subscription.deleted` the handler revokes the user's entire remaining credit balance, including credits purchased through the separate `credit_topup` checkout flow handled at line 23-25.
- **Risk:** Users lose separately-paid top-up value when a subscription lapses, which is a refund/chargeback and consumer-protection exposure for the waitlist-gated managed-cloud billing.
- **Fix:** Track subscription-allocated vs purchased top-up credits separately and only revoke the subscription-allocated portion on cancellation (or document/lock the forfeiture policy explicitly).

### [HIGH] data loss

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/user/delete-account/route.ts`
- **Line:** 70-94
- **Instance:** On ANY failure of the soft-delete UPDATE (including the guaranteed undefined-column error under the current schema or a transient DB outage) the fallback immediately and irreversibly hard-deletes the Clerk user, eliminating the promised 24-hour cancellation window.
- **Risk:** A transient database error converts a cancellable scheduled deletion into instant permanent account destruction with no grace period or recovery.

### [HIGH] incomplete wiring

- **Instance:** POST /devices/register stores device registrations in `sync_data` (sync_type 'device_registration'), but POST /batch validates device ownership against the separate `device_pairings` table (lines 108-114), so a device registered through this API will fail the H11 ownership check and get 403 on every batch sync.
- **Risk:** The documented client flow (register device, then sync_batch) is structurally broken in production — all batch syncs from newly registered devices are rejected.

### [HIGH] partial implementation

- **Line:** 256
- **Instance:** The schema accepts action 'Delete' (line 45) but the batch handler only ever inserts rows (lines 188-193), and GET /updates hardcodes `action: 'Update'` with an admission comment "we don't track action in schema".

### [HIGH] ignored promise

- **File:** `services/signaling-server/src/index.ts`
- **Line:** 1017
- **Instance:** Async `handleRegister()` is invoked fire-and-forget inside the WS message handler; when the rehydration DB query times out, the `Promise.race` rejection at line 1309 propagates through the awaited `pendingEntry.promise` (line 1339), rejects `handleRegister`'s unawaited promise, and lands in the process-level `unhandledRejection` handler (line 1213) which calls `gracefulShutdown()` and exits the process.
- **Risk:** A single slow/unresponsive Neon query (>10s) during a client register turns into a full signaling-server shutdown, disconnecting every paired desktop/mobile session.
- **Fix:** Wrap the `handleRegister(...)` call in `.catch()` (send an error to the socket and close it) so per-connection DB failures never reach the global unhandledRejection handler.

### [HIGH] fail-open behavior

- **File:** `crates/agiworkforce-protocol/src/protocol.rs`
- **Line:** 1251
- **Instance:** `SandboxPolicy::has_full_disk_read_access()` unconditionally returns `true`, ignoring the `ReadOnlyAccess::Restricted { readable_roots, .. }` configuration carried by the `ReadOnly` (line 1095) and `WorkspaceWrite` (line 1131) variants — a read-restricted policy reports full disk read access (the in-file test helper at line 4071 likewise allows reads everywhere).
- **Risk:** Any consumer that gates read-sandbox enforcement on this method silently skips the configured read restrictions, letting the agent read files outside the user-approved readable roots (fail-open on a security boundary).
- **Fix:** Return `false` (and consult `ReadOnlyAccess`/`get_readable_roots_with_cwd`) for `ReadOnly`/`WorkspaceWrite` variants whose read access is `Restricted`, or remove/deprecate the method so callers must use the access-aware APIs.

### [MEDIUM] fail-open behavior

- **Line:** 161
- **Instance:** `ShellEnvironmentPolicy::default()` sets `ignore_default_excludes: true` together with `inherit: All`, so the documented default exclude patterns `*KEY*`, `*SECRET*`, `*TOKEN*` (lines 128-141) are skipped and every child process spawned by the agent inherits all secret-bearing environment variables by default.

## Batch 076 — 20 files scanned

### [MEDIUM] excessive data exposure

- **File:** `crates/agiworkforce-protocol/src/shell_environment.rs`
- **Line:** 81-85
- **Instance:** Default secret-exclusion patterns only cover `*KEY*`, `*SECRET*`, and `*TOKEN*`, so common credential variables such as `*PASSWORD*`/`*PASSWD*` (e.g. `PGPASSWORD`), `*CREDENTIAL*`, and connection strings like `DATABASE_URL` pass into agent-driven shell subprocess environments.
- **Risk:** Agent-executed shell commands (and tool output echoed back into LLM context) can read live database/service passwords from the inherited environment, leaking secrets out of the Local trust boundary.
- **Fix:** Extend the default exclude list to `*PASSWORD*`, `*PASSWD*`, `*CREDENTIAL*` (and similar secret-name conventions) or make the core allowlist the default inherit policy.

### [LOW] silent failure

- **File:** `crates/agiworkforce-protocol/src/shell_environment.rs`
- **Line:** 94-102
- **Instance:** User-provided `policy.set` overrides (Step 4) are applied before the `include_only` retain (Step 5), so an explicitly `set` variable that does not match `include_only` is silently dropped.
- **Risk:** Users who configure both `set` and `include_only` lose explicitly requested env vars with no warning, producing confusing subprocess failures.
- **Fix:** Apply `set` after `include_only`, exempt explicitly-set keys from the filter, or document/log the precedence.

- **Risk:** Hashing large files serializes megabytes into a JSON number array (roughly 4x blowup), stalling the webview/IPC channel and spiking memory.

### [MEDIUM] frontend-secret exposure

- **Line:** 9-14
- **Instance:** `CalendarOAuthConfig` requires `clientSecret` to be present in renderer memory and passed through `calendarConnect` (line 81) on every connect, instead of referencing a backend-stored credential handle.
- **Risk:** OAuth client secrets live in webview JS state where any XSS/unsafe-rendering bug (e.g. in LLM-rendered content) can exfiltrate them.
- **Fix:** Store credentials once via a backend keychain-backed command and have `calendar_connect` accept a provider/account reference rather than the raw secret.

### [MEDIUM] fail-open behavior

- **File:** `packages/api/src/capabilities.ts`
- **Line:** 9
- **Instance:** `syncCapabilities` wholesale-replaces the backend capability map that gates tool execution (e.g. `fileOperations`, `terminalAccess` in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sys/commands/capabilities.rs`), where unknown/missing capabilities default to enabled, with no validation of capability keys.
- **Risk:** A partial or typo'd sync from the frontend silently re-enables every unsynced security gate (unknown keys default to true), so a UI regression can turn user-disabled tool restrictions back on.
- **Fix:** Validate synced keys against the known capability list on the Rust side and merge rather than replace, defaulting unknown security-relevant capabilities to their last persisted value instead of enabled.

## Batch 080 — 20 files scanned

### [MEDIUM] insecure-token-storage
- **File:** `packages/runtime/src/http.ts`
- **Line:** 24
- **Instance:** Cloud auth bearer token is read from `window.localStorage.getItem('agi-auth-token')`, meaning it is persisted in JS-readable web storage.
- **Risk:** Any XSS or third-party script in the web surface can exfiltrate the bearer token, granting full cloud-account access (token leakage / insecure token storage).
- **Fix:** Store the cloud auth token in an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie (or in-memory + silent refresh) rather than localStorage so injected scripts cannot read it.

### [MEDIUM] environment validation gap
- **File:** `packages/runtime/src/http.ts`
- **Line:** 11-20
- **Instance:** `getApiBaseUrl()` falls back to `http://localhost:3001/api` (plaintext HTTP) when neither `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` nor the `api-base-url` meta tag is present, with no validation that the resolved URL is HTTPS in production.
- **Risk:** If the env var/meta is missing in a production bundle, cloud commands silently POST the bearer token and command payloads over cleartext localhost or to an unintended origin (transport downgrade / log-leakage exposure).
- **Fix:** Require an explicit base URL in non-dev runtimes and reject non-HTTPS origins outside localhost/dev.

### [LOW] response validation gap
- **File:** `packages/runtime/src/http.ts`
- **Line:** 63-64
- **Instance:** The cloud response is cast directly as `{ data: T }` via `await response.json()` with no runtime shape validation before returning `result.data`.
- **Risk:** A malformed or hostile gateway response yields `undefined`/unexpected shapes that propagate as `T` and surface as confusing downstream type errors (malformed-response handling / unsafe API consumption).
- **Fix:** Validate the parsed envelope (presence of `data`, expected shape) before returning, throwing a typed error on mismatch.

### [HIGH] no-op logic

- **File:** `packages/runtime/src/state/onChangeAppState.ts`

### [HIGH] stale state

- **File:** `packages/runtime/src/offline-sync/index.ts`
- **Line:** 248
- **Instance:** `triggerSync` early-returns when `managerState.queuedCount === 0`, but `queuedCount` is only refreshed at `initialize`, after a completed sync, and via `queue.subscribeToQueueChanges` — and the queue's in-process mutations never notify subscribers (offline-queue `saveQueue` notifies no one; the web/desktop wiring uses the `window` `storage` event, which does not fire in the tab that performed the write).
- **Risk:** In the common single-tab flow — user queues messages while offline, connectivity returns, `handleOnline` calls `triggerSync` — the stale count of 0 aborts the sync and the queued messages are never sent until a reload or another tab mutates storage.

### [HIGH] lost update

- **File:** `packages/runtime/src/offline-queue/index.ts`
- **Line:** 271-275
- **Instance:** When `message.retryCount >= maxRetries` (default 3), `syncOfflineQueue` permanently deletes the user's queued message via `api.clearQueuedMessage` with only a `logger.warn` and an anonymous `messagesFailed++` counter — no dead-letter store and no callback identifying which message content was discarded.

- **Fix:** Move exhausted items to a dead-letter list (or mark them `failed` in place) and expose them through the API so the surface can show the content and offer manual retry/discard.

### [MEDIUM] authentication gap

- **File:** `packages/types/src/a2a.ts`
- **Line:** 103
- **Instance:** The A2A wire contract advertises HTTP and WebRTC transports (lines 9–11) and an `authRequired` flag on agent cards (line 75), yet `A2ATaskRequest` and `A2AHandoffRequest` carry only a self-asserted `fromAgent` string with no credential, token, or signature field anywhere in the protocol.
- **Risk:** Any networked A2A implementation built against this contract has no in-protocol way to verify the sender, so a spoofed `fromAgent` can delegate tasks or hand off full conversation history to/from agents it should not reach.
- **Fix:** Add an explicit auth envelope (e.g. `credentials?`/`signature?` field with a documented verification requirement) to task and handoff requests, or document that transport-level mutual auth is mandatory for non-`local://` endpoints.

### [MEDIUM] authentication gap

- **File:** `packages/types/src/pairing.ts`
- **Line:** 41
- **Instance:** The cross-device pairing contract uses a low-entropy 6-digit numeric `code` as the sole pairing credential, with no field for a key fingerprint, SAS verification, or signed token binding the mobile peer to the desktop.
- **Risk:** If the signaling server does not aggressively rate-limit, a 6-digit code (1M combinations, 5-minute window) is brute-forceable, letting an attacker pair a rogue device to a victim desktop and receive approval/monitor/voice capabilities.
- **Fix:** Extend the contract with a high-entropy secret or public-key fingerprint field (and verify it during the WebRTC handshake) so the short code is only a discovery hint, not the trust anchor.

## Batch 085 — 20 files scanned

### [HIGH] stale state

- **File:** `packages/utils/src/errors.ts`
- **Line:** 750
- **Instance:** `getContextualError` mutates `friendly.suggestion` on the object returned by `getFriendlyError`, but when the error is an `AppError` that object is the shared `ERROR_CODE_MESSAGES[code]` constant returned by reference from `getFriendlyErrorByCode` (line 297), so the mutation permanently rewrites the global error-message table for all subsequent callers (also mutated at lines 759 and 764).
- **Risk:** After one contextual call, every future user of that error code sees the wrong, context-specific (or "cannot be retried") suggestion process-wide — a cross-request state corruption bug that will fire in production.
- **Fix:** Have `getFriendlyErrorByCode` return a shallow copy (`{ ...ERROR_CODE_MESSAGES[code] }`) or clone `friendly` in `getContextualError` before mutating.

### [MEDIUM] prompt injection

- **File:** `packages/utils/src/fence.ts`
- **Line:** 32
- **Instance:** The fence-tag strip `replace(new RegExp(\`</?${tag}>\`, 'gi'), '')` is single-pass and non-recursive, so nested payloads like `</</tag>tag>` have the inner `</tag>` removed and the remaining characters reassemble into a live `</tag>`, escaping the trust-boundary fence.
- **Risk:** Untrusted content (user memory, web content) can close the fence tag and inject instructions into the system prompt despite the sanitizer.
- **Fix:** Loop the replacement until no match remains (fixed-point sanitization) or escape `<`/`>` inside fenced content instead of deleting tag literals.

### [MEDIUM] validation bypass

- **File:** `packages/utils/src/fence.ts`
- **Line:** 15
- **Instance:** The invisible-character strip covers zero-width/BOM/bidi embeddings and isolates but omits known invisible prompt-injection vectors: the Unicode Tags block (U+E0000–E007F "ASCII smuggling"), U+061C (Arabic letter mark, a bidi control), U+2060 (word joiner), and U+00AD (soft hyphen); the tag strip on line 32 also misses variants like `</tag >` or `</tag\t>` that LLMs commonly treat as closing tags.
- **Risk:** Attackers can smuggle invisible instructions or escape the fence with whitespace-variant closing tags, defeating the module's stated injection protection.
- **Fix:** Extend the regex to include U+00AD, U+061C, U+2060, U+180E and U+E0000–U+E007F, and make the tag-strip regex tolerate whitespace/attributes (`</?\s*tag[^>]*>`).

### [MEDIUM] insecure token storage

- **File:** `packages/utils/src/crypto.ts`
- **Line:** 129
- **Instance:** `generateNumericCode`, documented for OTP/pairing/verification codes, maps random bytes with `b % 10`, which has modulo bias (256 % 10 = 6) making digits 0–5 statistically more likely than 6–9.
- **Risk:** OTP and pairing codes have measurably reduced entropy, marginally easing brute-force of verification codes used at trust boundaries.
- **Fix:** Use rejection sampling (discard bytes >= 250) or `crypto.getRandomValues` over a Uint32 range reduction that eliminates bias.

### [LOW] edge-case blindness

- **File:** `packages/utils/src/crypto.ts`

- **Instance:** `generateShortId` uses `b % alphabet.length` with a 62-character alphabet (256 % 62 = 8), so the first 8 alphabet characters are slightly over-represented in generated IDs/share codes.
- **Risk:** Share-link identifiers have slightly less entropy than their length implies, weakening unguessability guarantees marginally.
- **Fix:** Use rejection sampling or a power-of-two alphabet (e.g., 64 chars) so the modulo is bias-free.

- **Instance:** `validateUrl`'s `blockPrivateNetworks` guard matches only dotted-decimal private ranges, so encoded loopback/metadata addresses bypass it: `http://2130706433/` (decimal 127.0.0.1), `http://0x7f.0.0.1/`, `http://0/`, and IPv4-mapped IPv6 like `http://[::ffff:169.254.169.254]/` all pass validation.
- **Risk:** Callers relying on this helper as an SSRF guard can be tricked into fetching internal services or cloud metadata endpoints via integer/hex/IPv6-mapped address encodings.
- **Fix:** Normalize the hostname to a canonical IP (parse integer/hex/octal forms and IPv4-mapped IPv6) before comparing against the private-range patterns, and reject `0.0.0.0`/`[::]`.

### [MEDIUM] security theater

- **File:** `packages/utils/src/validation.ts`
- **Line:** 318
- **Instance:** `sanitizeCommandArgs` strips shell metacharacters with a denylist but leaves the rest intact, so its own JSDoc example turns `'; rm -rf /'` into `' rm -rf /'` — still a destructive command if the "sanitized" arg is ever concatenated into a shell string.
- **Risk:** The function name implies command-injection safety, encouraging callers to interpolate its output into shells where the surviving tokens remain dangerous (and legitimate args containing `&`/`*` are silently corrupted).
- **Fix:** Pass arguments as an argv array to spawn without a shell (allowlist execution) rather than denylist character stripping, and rename/document the helper to reflect it is not an injection guard.

### [LOW] security theater

- **File:** `packages/utils/src/validation.ts`

- **Instance:** `checkForInjection`'s SQL pattern flags any input containing the bare words SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/CREATE/ALTER (word-boundary, case-insensitive), so ordinary prose like "please update my profile" is reported as `SQL Injection`.
- **Risk:** Extremely high false-positive rate makes the check unusable as a gate and gives a false sense of protection (it is disclaimed but exported as a public API).
- **Fix:** Rely on parameterized queries and remove/rescope this heuristic to clearly non-security telemetry, or require injection-shaped context (quotes + operators) before flagging.

### [LOW] edge-case blindness

- **File:** `packages/utils/src/validation.ts`
- **Line:** 120
- **Instance:** `validateFilePath` rejects any path containing the substring `..` (so a legitimate filename like `report..final.txt` is blocked) and only denylists a fixed set of system directories without normalizing the path first.
- **Risk:** Valid paths are rejected (availability) while non-listed sensitive locations (e.g., user dotfiles) are allowed, and the unnormalized check can be bypassed by mixed separators.
- **Fix:** Resolve/normalize the path and use a separator-aware traversal check (reuse `resolveContained` from `pathContainment.ts`) plus an allowlist root rather than substring matching.

- **File:** `packages/utils/src/signaling.ts`
- **Line:** 252
- **Instance:** The default branch logs the entire unknown incoming message object via `console.warn` (also lines 154 and 186), bypassing the package's secret-redacting `logger` facade; WebRTC signaling messages can carry SDP/ICE candidate data (local IPs) and arbitrary `payload`.

- **Fix:** Route these through `logger.warn` (which redacts) and log only the message `type`, not the full object.

### [LOW] timeout omission

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/api/accountApi.ts`
- **Line:** 33
- **Instance:** `withTimeout` races against a `setTimeout` whose handle is never cleared, so a pending 30–60s timer survives after the underlying invoke resolves (unlike the cleared-timer implementation in `packages/utils/src/async.ts`).

- **Fix:** Capture the timer id and `clearTimeout` it in a `.finally()` on the race, as the shared `withTimeout` in `async.ts` already does.

## Batch 089 — 20 files scanned

### [HIGH] session confusion

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/hooks/useDeepLink.ts`
- **Line:** 181
- **Instance:** The `auth-callback` deep link handler immediately calls `cloudAccountAuth.exchangeCodeForSession(code)` with an attacker-triggerable code (any web page can launch `agiworkforce://auth/callback?code=...`) and `parseDeepLink` (lines 109-120) never requires or validates an OAuth `state` parameter for this path, unlike the MCP OAuth path which carries state through.
- **Risk:** If the exchange is not bound to a locally stored PKCE verifier/state, an attacker can force the victim's desktop app into a session for an attacker-controlled cloud account (login CSRF / session fixation), causing subsequent chats and synced data to land in the attacker's account.
- **Fix:** Require and validate a `state` value bound to a locally initiated auth flow (and confirm PKCE verifier binding) before exchanging any deep-link-supplied code.

### [HIGH] empty-state bug

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/hooks/useCreditRefresh.ts`
- **Line:** 65
- **Instance:** `hasCredits = monthly_remaining_cents > 0` gates the entire store update and warning block (and again at line 164 in `refreshCreditsAfterMessage`), so once credits reach exactly zero the account store is never updated and no depletion warning is shown.
- **Risk:** Users who fully exhaust credits see a stale non-zero balance and never receive the "depleted" notification — the exact moment the hook exists for is the one case it skips.
- **Fix:** Always write the fetched balance to the store and add an explicit zero/exhausted branch that surfaces a depletion warning.

### [HIGH] stale state

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/hooks/useLSP.ts`
- **Line:** 92
- **Instance:** When the `language`/`rootPath` props change, the effect cleanup (lines 425-435) stops the old server but never clears `server`/`serverRef`, so the re-run's `startServer` hits the `if (isStartingRef.current || serverRef.current) return;` guard and never starts the new language's server.
- **Risk:** After any language switch the hook permanently reports a stale `server` object for a stopped server and all LSP features (completions, hover, diagnostics) silently dead-end via their `if (!server) return` guards against a dead backend.
- **Fix:** Reset `setServer(null)` and `serverRef.current = null` in the effect cleanup (or key the guard by language) so a dependency change restarts the server.

### [MEDIUM] async race

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/hooks/useAgenticEvents.ts`
- **Line:** 1572
- **Instance:** `initializeRuntimeActivityEventListeners` can be re-entered after `cleanupRuntimeActivityEventListeners` runs while the first `setupRuntimeActivityEventListeners` is still awaiting Tauri `listen` calls (cleanup nulls `initializationPromise` and resets flags without cancelling or awaiting the in-flight setup), so a remount (e.g. React StrictMode) registers a second full set of listeners alongside the still-registering first set, and line 1585 re-activates both.
- **Risk:** Duplicate active listeners process every agentic event twice, producing doubled action-log entries, trail entries, and store updates.
- **Fix:** Have cleanup await/cancel the in-flight initialization promise, or generation-tag each setup and immediately unlisten registrations from a stale generation.

# Batch 093 — 20 files scanned

### [MEDIUM] no-op logic

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/lib/toolMatcher.ts`
- **Line:** 643
- **Instance:** `hasRequiredTools` returns true as soon as ANY single required category is satisfied (early `return true` inside the loop) instead of requiring ALL required categories, and since `BUILT_IN_TOOLS` statically covers every category the function can never return false.
- **Risk:** Callers believe required tooling is present when one of several required categories is missing, so intents like `coding` (requires code-execution AND file-system) proceed without their full toolset.
- **Fix:** Invert the logic to return false when any required category has no built-in or MCP tool (mirror `getMissingToolCategories`), and only count tools that are actually registered at runtime.

### [MEDIUM] tool poisoning

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/lib/toolMatcher.ts`
- **Line:** 552-559
- **Instance:** MCP tool relevance is boosted to 0.6 whenever any 4+ character word from the third-party tool's self-supplied description appears in the user message (`term.length > 3 && lowerMessage.includes(term)`), with no stop-word filtering or trust weighting.
- **Risk:** A malicious or sloppy MCP server can stuff common words ("with", "your", "file", "search") into its description to get itself suggested/auto-selected for nearly every user message — a classic MCP tool-poisoning vector.
- **Fix:** Match only against curated keywords or the tool name, apply a stop-word list, and never let third-party-controlled description text raise relevance above category-based scores.

### [MEDIUM] approval-gate gap

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/lib/toolMatcher.ts`
- **Line:** 575-577
- **Instance:** `autoExecute` is set to true purely from keyword/category heuristics on the user message (any required-category match with relevance > 0.7) and is propagated to `modelRouter`'s `autoExecuteTools` without any consent or risk-tier consideration.
- **Risk:** Side-effectful tools (browser actions, email_send, file writes) can be flagged for automatic execution off a single keyword match, eroding the human-in-the-loop gate if any consumer honors the flag directly.
- **Fix:** Gate `autoExecute` on a per-tool risk classification and the user's approval settings, never on message keyword heuristics alone.

### [CRITICAL] fail-open behavior

- **File:** `apps/web/features/chat/lib/localByokHandoff.ts`
- **Line:** 110-118
- **Instance:** `shouldForkLocalToByok` returns false whenever the source provider mode cannot be inferred (`getConversationProviderMode` returns null for unmapped local model IDs, e.g. a bare Ollama model name without an `ollama/` prefix and no metadata), so the Local-to-BYOK fork/consent gate is silently skipped and the conversation continues straight onto the BYOK provider.
- **Risk:** Local conversation content is silently routed across the Local/BYOK trust boundary without the required context selection, secret scan, payload preview, and consent — a locked-rule trust-boundary break.
- **Fix:** Treat an unresolvable source mode as Local (fail closed) when the target mode is `DirectByok`, or block the send until the source mode can be determined.

### [MEDIUM] unsafe casting

- **File:** `apps/web/features/chat/lib/localByokHandoff.ts`
- **Line:** 87-91
- **Instance:** `message.metadata?.providerMode` is cast to `ProviderMode` with only a `typeof === 'string'` check, so any miscased or stale string (e.g. `'local'` instead of `'Local'`) is accepted and short-circuits model-based inference.
- **Risk:** A corrupted or differently-cased metadata value makes `sourceMode === 'Local'` false and bypasses the BYOK fork consent gate the same way as the fail-open above.
- **Fix:** Validate the metadata value against the ProviderMode union ('Local' | 'DirectByok' | 'ManagedGateway' | 'ManagedNative') before trusting it, falling through to model inference otherwise.

### [HIGH] stale state

- **File:** `apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-voice-recording.ts`
- **Line:** 170-178
- **Instance:** The "cleanup on unmount" effect is keyed on `[cleanup, audioUrl]`, so its teardown also runs whenever `audioUrl` changes; starting a second recording calls `setAudioUrl(null)` (line 396) which fires the previous effect's cleanup and `cleanup()` stops the just-created MediaStream tracks, closes the new AudioContext, and clears `mediaRecorderRef`/`chunksRef`.
- **Risk:** Every recording after the first is killed immediately (tracks stopped → recorder stops with empty chunks), so re-recording is broken in production.
- **Fix:** Split the effect: a mount-only effect (empty deps) for `cleanup()`, and track the latest `audioUrl` in a ref for URL revocation on unmount only.

### [HIGH] silent failure

- **File:** `apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-voice-recording.ts`
- **Line:** 438-452
- **Instance:** `stopRecording` wraps `onstop` and first invokes the original handler (lines 359-373) which calls `cleanup()` — clearing `chunksRef.current` to `[]` (line 166) — and only then builds the promise's resolved Blob from the now-empty `chunksRef.current` inside the 50ms `setTimeout`.
- **Risk:** Callers that `await stopRecording()` receive an empty audio blob, losing the entire recording on any flow that consumes the returned value (e.g. send-voice-message).
- **Fix:** Capture the chunks (or build the Blob) before calling the original onstop/cleanup, or resolve with the same Blob the original handler constructed.

### [HIGH] stale closure

- **File:** `apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-voice-recording.ts`
- **Line:** 236
- **Instance:** The first `requestAnimationFrame(updateAudioLevels)` scheduled at line 407 invokes the closure created while `isRecording` was still false, so the guard `!isRecording` returns before scheduling the next frame via `updateAudioLevelsRef`, and the visualization loop never starts (the resume path at line 490 has the analogous stale `isPaused === true` closure).
- **Risk:** `audioLevels` is never populated, so the recording waveform/level visualization is dead every time in production.
- **Fix:** Drive the loop's guard from refs (e.g. `isRecordingRef`) instead of closed-over state, or kick the loop from an effect that runs after `isRecording` becomes true.

### [MEDIUM] stale closure

### [HIGH] excessive data exposure

- **File:** `apps/web/features/chat/services/attachment-handler.ts`
- **Line:** 129
- **Instance:** Chat attachments are uploaded to Vercel Blob with `access: 'public'`, the header comment (line 8) confirms the URLs are permanent, and `refreshSignedUrl` (lines 305-307) is a no-op returning the same URL — there is no expiry, auth, or revocation short of deletion.

### [MEDIUM] server-client boundary violation

- **File:** `apps/web/features/chat/services/attachment-handler.ts`
- **Line:** 136
- **Instance:** `uploadFile` calls the server-only `@vercel/blob` `put()` (needs BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN, line 13) and in the same call path invokes `createThumbnail` which uses browser-only DOM APIs (`document.createElement`, `Image`, `URL.createObjectURL`, lines 173-183), and `downloadFile` (lines 365-371) is also DOM-only.

- **Fix:** Split into a server upload service (blob SDK) and a client helper (thumbnail/download), with the client posting files to an authenticated upload API route.

## Batch 103 — 20 files scanned

### [HIGH] IDOR

- **File:** `apps/web/features/chat/stores/artifacts-store.ts`
- **Line:** 363
- **Instance:** `shareArtifact` generates the share capability ID with `share-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).substr(2, 9)}` — non-cryptographic randomness for a share token, while the same file uses `crypto.randomUUID()` elsewhere (line 212), and the client-minted ID is sent to the server as `share_id`.
- **Risk:** Math.random output is predictable (CWE-338), so shared-artifact IDs can be guessed/enumerated, exposing other users' shared artifact content via the publish/share endpoint.
- **Fix:** Mint share IDs server-side with a CSPRNG (or at minimum use `crypto.randomUUID()` on the client) and never accept a client-supplied share ID.

- **Risk:** Users copy and distribute a share link that resolves to nothing because the artifact was never persisted server-side.
- **Fix:** Throw or return a failure result when persistence does not succeed, and only attach `shareId` after a confirmed 2xx response.

### [MEDIUM] async race

### [MEDIUM] hardcoded secret

- **File:** `apps/web/features/settings/services/user-preferences.ts`
- **Line:** 69
- **Instance:** `getConfiguredTOTPKeyMaterial` builds the AES-256-GCM key by UTF-8-encoding the first 32 characters of the `TOTP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` env string with no KDF — printable-ASCII key material yields far less than 256 bits of entropy, and any ≥32-char string is accepted (this code is live: the 2FA server routes import `encryptTOTPSecret`/`decryptTOTPSecret` from this module).
- **Risk:** TOTP secrets at rest are protected by a key materially weaker than AES-256 assumes, easing offline decryption if the database leaks alongside a guessable/low-entropy env value.
- **Fix:** Derive the key with HKDF/PBKDF2 from the env secret (or require a base64-encoded 32-byte random key) and validate its entropy at startup.

### [HIGH] SSRF
- **File:** `apps/web/lib/egress-policy.ts`
- **Line:** 74-81
- **Instance:** `isInternalHostname` IPv6 branch only rejects `::1`, `fc/fd` (ULA) and `fe8-b` (link-local) prefixes and returns `false` for everything else, so IPv4-mapped IPv6 literals like `::ffff:169.254.169.254` (and non-dotted IPv4 like decimal `2130706433`) are not normalized and are treated as public.
- **Risk:** A user-supplied image URL such as `https://[::ffff:169.254.169.254]/latest/meta-data/` passes `validateUserImageUrl`/`assertNonInternalHostname` (and `assertResolvedPublicHostname` early-returns at line 116 because `isIP` reports a valid IPv6), letting the provider image fetcher reach AWS IMDS / internal services — the exact SSRF amplification the module exists to prevent (WEB-MULTIMODAL-IMAGE-SSRF).
- **Fix:** Normalize IPv4-mapped/compatible IPv6 to their embedded IPv4 and re-run the IPv4 private/loopback checks, and reject non-dotted IPv4 notations (decimal/octal/hex) before allowing the host.

### [HIGH] open redirect

- **File:** `apps/web/lib/safe-redirect.ts`
- **Line:** 124
- **Instance:** `isRedirectSafe` approves any string starting with a single `/` (e.g. `/\evil.com`), but browsers normalize backslash to forward slash so `/\evil.com` becomes the protocol-relative URL `//evil.com`; unlike `getSafeRedirectUrl`, this function returns the verdict without sanitizing, so a caller redirecting to the raw value is exploitable.
- **Risk:** Attacker-supplied `?redirect=/\evil.com` passes the safety check and sends users to an attacker-controlled host (phishing/token theft).
- **Fix:** Reject paths whose second character is `\` (or normalize backslashes to `/` before the `//` check) in `isRedirectSafe`, mirroring a parse-and-inspect approach like `getSafeRedirectUrl`.

- **File:** `apps/web/lib/validations/path.ts`
- **Line:** 11, 32, 49
- **Instance:** The module-level `DANGEROUS_PATH_CHARS` regex is declared with the global `g` flag (line 11, kept "for .replace()") but is also reused with `.test()` in `SafePathSchema` (line 32) and `SafeFileNameSchema` (line 49); a global regex retains `lastIndex` across `.test()` calls, so after any rejected path the next validation starts mid-string and can return a false negative, letting paths/filenames containing `\0 < > : " | ? *` pass this security validator on alternating calls.
- **Risk:** An attacker (or just normal interleaved traffic on a warm serverless instance) can slip null-byte or otherwise dangerous path characters past validation, weakening the path-traversal/injection defense everywhere `SafePathSchema`, `SafeFileNameSchema`, or `isPathSafe` is used standalone.

- **Risk:** Non-vision/non-tool local models (e.g., small Ollama models) are advertised as vision- and tool-capable with 128k context, so users attach images or trigger tools that fail at request time.
- **Fix:** Source `supportsVision`/`supportsTools`/`contextWindow` from `packages/types/src/models.json`-backed metadata (as the fallback path at line 765 already does) instead of hardcoding.

### [LOW] magic constants

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx`
- **Line:** 685
- **Instance:** Model `tier` and `supportsThinking` are inferred from name substrings ("opus", "4o", "pro", "haiku", "mini", "flash", "think") and `provider === 'anthropic'` heuristics.
- **Risk:** New or renamed models get mis-tiered and mislabeled for thinking support, drifting silently from the canonical catalog as model names change.
- **Fix:** Read tier/thinking capability from the shared model catalog metadata rather than name-substring heuristics.

### [MEDIUM] contract drift

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx`
- **Line:** 682
- **Instance:** Any backend-reported provider not in the hardcoded `validProviders` set is silently coerced to `'openai'` when building the chat model list (repeated at line 721 in the web fallback).
- **Risk:** In a product where the visible provider label is a locked trust-boundary rule, a new/unlisted provider gets displayed as OpenAI, showing users a false provider attribution.
- **Fix:** Pass unknown providers through (widening the ModelInfo type) or mark them as an explicit `'unknown'` provider instead of defaulting to `'openai'`.

### [MEDIUM] async race

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx`
- **Line:** 707
- **Instance:** The `initModels` effect re-runs on every `appMode` change with no cancellation/abort, so a slow in-flight run for the previous mode can resolve last and overwrite `useChatModelStore.setModels` after the user has switched modes.
- **Risk:** The model picker can display the prior mode's list (e.g., local/BYOK models while in managed-cloud mode, or vice versa), a stale trust-boundary-labeled UI state.
- **Fix:** Track a cancellation flag (or AbortController) in the effect and skip `setModels` when the captured mode no longer matches the current `appMode`.

### [LOW] response validation gap

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx`
- **Line:** 718
- **Instance:** The web-mode fallback maps `/api/models` response items straight into the chat store with only an `Array.isArray` check — `id`/`name` are unvalidated and `provider` is cast to the ModelInfo provider union without the `validProviders` whitelist used on the primary path, and the fetch has no timeout.
- **Risk:** A malformed or slow API response yields undefined-labeled or arbitrarily-typed provider entries in the model picker and a hung fallback path.
- **Fix:** Validate each model object's fields (and reuse the provider whitelist) before `setModels`, and wrap the fetch with an AbortController timeout.

### [LOW] symptom patching

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx`
- **Line:** 301
- **Instance:** The global unhandled-rejection handler string-matches `listeners[eventId]` to suppress a "known Tauri internal" error instead of fixing or scoping the underlying event-cleanup bug.
- **Risk:** The substring filter can silently swallow unrelated future rejections whose messages happen to contain that token, hiding real failures from the error store.
- **Fix:** Fix the event-listener cleanup ordering that produces the error (or scope the suppression to the exact known error type) and add a tracked issue reference.

### [LOW] edge-case blindness

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx`
- **Line:** 909
- **Instance:** The `zoom_in`/`zoom_out` menu actions multiply the root font-size by 1.1 with no clamp on minimum or maximum.
- **Risk:** Repeated zoom presses drive the UI to unusably huge or microscopic text (and the value persists until "actual size" is found), an accessibility trap.
- **Fix:** Clamp the computed font-size to a sane range (e.g., 50%–200% of the base size).

## Batch 115 — 20 files scanned

### [HIGH] contract drift

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agent-collaboration/AgentCollaborationPanel.tsx`
- **Line:** 143
- **Instance:** Frontend listens for events `swarm:progress` (line 143), `swarm:agent_message` (line 150), and `swarm:complete` (line 169), but the Rust backend only emits `swarm:started`, `swarm:decomposed`, `swarm:completed`, `swarm:subtask_started/completed/failed` (src-tauri/src/core/swarm/orchestrator.rs:187-606), so none of these listeners ever fire.
- **Risk:** The agent list, agent-to-agent message feed, and swarm-complete result capture are permanently dead in production — the panel renders empty forever while a swarm actually runs.
- **Fix:** Align event names with the backend emits (or add the missing emits in orchestrator.rs) and add an integration test that asserts each listened event has a Rust fire site.

### [HIGH] API contract violation

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agent-collaboration/AgentCollaborationPanel.tsx`
- **Line:** 198
- **Instance:** `invoke('swarm_init', { request: { maxAgents, autoSpawn, optimizeCriticalPath } })` sends camelCase keys, but Rust `SwarmInitRequest` (src-tauri/src/sys/commands/swarm.rs:30-35) declares snake_case fields `max_agents/auto_spawn/optimize_critical_path` with no `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`, so deserialization fails.
- **Risk:** The "Init Swarm" button always errors in the real desktop app, making the entire Agent Collaboration feature unusable.
- **Fix:** Add `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` to `SwarmInitRequest` (or send snake_case keys from the frontend) and cover the command with a round-trip test.

### [HIGH] contract drift

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agent-collaboration/AgentCollaborationPanel.tsx`
- **Line:** 77
- **Instance:** The frontend `SwarmResult` interface expects camelCase `goalId/wallTime/speedupRatio/criticalPathLength/maxParallelism` with `wallTime` as a number, but Rust `SwarmResult` (orchestrator.rs:96-119) serializes snake_case fields and `wall_time` as a `Duration` struct (`{secs, nanos}`).
- **Risk:** Every results card renders "N/A"/undefined for wall time, speedup, parallelism, and critical path even on successful runs.
- **Fix:** Add `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` plus a millisecond serializer for `wall_time` on the Rust struct, or update the TS interface to the actual wire shape.

### [HIGH] contract drift

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agent-collaboration/AgentCollaborationPanel.tsx`
- **Line:** 59
- **Instance:** Frontend `SwarmStats` expects `totalAgents/activeAgents/completedTasks/failedTasks/averageLatencyMs`, but Rust `SwarmStats` (orchestrator.rs:71-86) serializes `goals_processed/subtasks_created/subtasks_completed/subtasks_failed/peak_agents/avg_speedup_ratio/total_wall_time_ms` — zero overlapping field names.
- **Risk:** The stats bar (lines 797-807) renders "undefined completed / undefined failed / Avg latency: undefinedms" whenever stats load.
- **Fix:** Define a shared serde-camelCase stats DTO matching the TS interface and map the orchestrator fields into it.

### [HIGH] mock leakage

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agent-collaboration/AgentCollaborationPanel.tsx`
- **Line:** 220
- **Instance:** `invoke('swarm_execute_goal', ...)` is not gated on `isTauri` (only the listeners are, line 132), and the shared `tauri-mock` shim returns `{ success: true, output: '(mock swarm result)' }` for this command in cloud-web/dev fallthrough (src/lib/tauri-mock.ts:1133-1140).
- **Risk:** In non-Tauri (cloud web) builds a user pressing Execute sees "Completed Successfully" with fabricated results while nothing actually ran — fake completion presented as real output.
- **Fix:** Gate the panel (or its invokes) on `isTauri` with an explicit "requires desktop app" state instead of letting mock success values render as results.

### [MEDIUM] implementation theater

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agent-collaboration/AgentCollaborationPanel.tsx`
- **Line:** 268
- **Instance:** "Task delegation" to a specific agent is implemented by prefixing the goal string with `[Agent: ${agent.name}]` and calling the generic `swarm_execute_goal`, which spawns a fresh swarm goal rather than routing the task to the selected agent.
- **Risk:** The UI claims a task was assigned to a chosen agent while the backend ignores the selection, misleading users observing multi-agent workflows.
- **Fix:** Add a real backend command that targets a specific agent id (or remove the per-agent selector until it exists).

### [MEDIUM] lost update

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agent-collaboration/AgentCollaborationPanel.tsx`
- **Line:** 274
- **Instance:** The `.then()` after `swarm_execute_goal` unconditionally sets the delegation status to `running`, but the invoke resolves only when the goal has finished, and it overwrites a `completed` status that the `swarm:agent_message` result handler (lines 155-163) may have set.
- **Risk:** Delegations are displayed as perpetually "running" after they finish, and a completed status can be regressed back to running.
- **Fix:** Set status to `running` before/immediately after dispatch and mark `completed` (guarding against status downgrades) when the invoke resolves.

### [MEDIUM] request validation gap

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agent-collaboration/AgentCollaborationPanel.tsx`
- **Line:** 426
- **Instance:** The max-agents input uses `parseInt(e.target.value) || 5` without clamping to the declared 1-20 range (HTML `min`/`max` do not constrain typed values), and the value is sent straight to `swarm_init`.
- **Risk:** A typed value like 999 requests an unbounded agent swarm, risking resource exhaustion once the init contract bug is fixed.
- **Fix:** Clamp the parsed value to [1, 20] before storing it in state and validate `max_agents` server-side in the Rust command.

### [MEDIUM] hardcoded success

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agi/AgentTaskMonitor.tsx`
- **Line:** 117-124
- **Instance:** `handleCancel` fires `toast.success('Task cancelled')` unconditionally after `await cancelTask(...)`, but the store's `cancelTask` (agentTaskStore.ts:441-459) swallows invoke errors internally and never rethrows, so the component's catch branch is dead and the success toast shows even when cancellation failed.
- **Risk:** User sees "Task cancelled" while the agent task is actually still running, contradicting the simultaneous store-level error toast and masking a failed cancel of an autonomous agent.

### [MEDIUM] unsafe markdown rendering

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/artifacts/MarkdownArtifact.tsx`
- **Line:** 24
- **Instance:** Untrusted LLM-generated artifact markdown is rendered via ReactMarkdown with no `components.a` override and no global click interceptor (verified none in App.tsx/main.tsx), so a click on a rendered anchor navigates the Tauri webview itself to an arbitrary external URL.
- **Risk:** A malicious or hallucinated link in artifact content replaces the app window with an attacker page (phishing surface that escapes the app CSP), losing app state — unlike sibling surfaces (ResearchReport etc.) that route links through openUrl/target=\_blank.
- **Fix:** Override the `a` renderer to open links via the Tauri opener/shell plugin (with URL-scheme allowlist) instead of allowing in-webview navigation.

- **Risk:** Theme switches and brand re-skins silently miss these literals, producing inconsistent/unreadable UI in non-default themes.

### [MEDIUM] semantic incorrectness

### [MEDIUM] security theater

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/artifacts/SvgArtifact.tsx`

### [CRITICAL] tenant isolation failure

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/ChatInputArea.tsx`
- **Line:** 1051
- **Instance:** `handleSubmit` silently rewrites `providerOverride` to `'managed_cloud'` for any user on a managed plan whenever `selectedProvider !== 'ollama'`, which reroutes chats the user explicitly pointed at the local `lmstudio` provider (declared Local in `apps/desktop/src/types/provider.ts:18`) or at an explicit BYOK provider (anthropic/openai/etc.) into managed cloud with no consent flow, no payload preview, and no fork/continuation step.
- **Risk:** Local-only conversations and BYOK-keyed conversations are silently routed across the Local/BYOK/Managed-Cloud trust boundary — a direct violation of the locked product rule "Never silently route Local chats, files, or developer sessions to BYOK or managed cloud."
- **Fix:** Only apply the managed_cloud override when the user actually selected the managed_cloud/auto provider; exempt all local providers (`ollama`, `lmstudio`) and never override an explicit BYOK provider selection — route changes must go through the explicit fork/consent flow.

### [CRITICAL] tenant isolation failure

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/ChatInputArea.tsx`
- **Line:** 524
- **Instance:** `sendPendingMessage` (the queued-message auto-send path) duplicates the same silent override — `isManagedPlan && selectedProvider !== 'ollama' ? 'managed_cloud' : ...` — so queued messages composed against a local `lmstudio` or BYOK provider are auto-sent to managed cloud with zero user interaction at send time.
- **Risk:** Queued messages cross the Local/BYOK → Managed-Cloud trust boundary fully automatically (the user is not even present at the moment of send), leaking local-only content to the cloud backend.
- **Fix:** Share one provider-resolution helper that never overrides local or BYOK selections to managed_cloud without the explicit consent flow, and use it in both send paths.

### [HIGH] human-in-the-loop gap

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/ChatInputArea.tsx`
- **Line:** 840
- **Instance:** `detectAndCaptureScreen` regex-matches phrases like "what's on my screen" in the typed message and, on match (invoked from `handleSubmit` at line 932), auto-captures the full screen via `capture_screen_full` and sends it as an attachment in the same submit, with no confirmation or preview step before the capture leaves the machine.
- **Risk:** Screen contents (other apps, secrets, passwords, private messages visible on screen) are captured and uploaded to whatever provider the message routes to — including managed cloud via the line-1051 override — based solely on a text pattern, a PII-leakage path across trust boundaries without explicit user approval.
- **Fix:** Require an explicit user confirmation (or at minimum a visible pre-send preview with cancel) before auto-captured screenshots are attached and sent.

### [HIGH] insecure output handling

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/GenerativeWidget.tsx`
- **Line:** 49
- **Instance:** The CSP for LLM-generated widget HTML sets `connect-src 'none'` but allows `img-src data: https:` and `font-src https:`, so AI-authored markup can issue GET requests to arbitrary HTTPS hosts via `<img>`/`@font-face` URLs.
- **Risk:** Indirect prompt injection (e.g., poisoned web content in a prior tool result) can make the model emit a widget that exfiltrates conversation data to an attacker host through image-URL query strings — the classic markdown-image exfil channel this CSP otherwise tries to block.
- **Fix:** Restrict `img-src` to `data:` plus the same allow-listed CDN origins (and `font-src` likewise), or proxy remote images.

### [MEDIUM] message-validation gap

- **Instance:** The comment claims "Only accept messages from our own blob URL origin" but `handleMessage` (lines 136-150) never checks `event.source`/`event.origin`, accepting any `widget-resize` message on the window.
- **Risk:** With multiple widgets rendered, every instance resizes on any widget's message (cross-talk), and any embedded frame can spoof resize messages to distort the chat layout; the comment is security theater.
- **Fix:** Accept only messages where `event.source === iframeRef.current?.contentWindow` and clamp height to a sane positive range.

- **Line:** 357
- **Instance:** The SendPreview privacy banner computes `providerMode` from `selectedProvider` only (`!providerKey ? 'Local'`, lines 358-366), but the actual send path falls back to `llmConfig.defaultProvider` (lines 518-519, 902) — so with no explicit selection and a default provider of `managed_cloud` or a BYOK provider, the banner displays "Local" while the message is routed to cloud; per-send `options.providerOverride` is also never reflected in the banner.
