- **Line:** 24
- **Instance:** The `~/.ssh` and `~/.gnupg` read-rejection tests only assert when the directory `.exists()`, so on a machine without those dirs they pass without exercising the protection.

### [LOW] mock leakage

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/core/agi/tests/planner_tests.rs`

- **Risk:** If the real `calculate_plan_duration` changes (e.g. a future regression reorders the CPU thresholds the comments warn about for bug #48), the mirror stays green and the regression ships undetected — the test cannot actually catch the bug it claims to guard.
- **Fix:** Call the production `AGIPlanner` duration/multiplier logic directly (expose a testable function if needed) so the test fails when the real implementation drifts.

### [HIGH] security theater

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/core/agi/tests/security_tests.rs`
- **Line:** 4-93
- **Instance:** The entire security suite defines a private mock `SecurityValidator` (with its own `validate_path`, `validate_command`, `detect_prompt_injection`) inside the test file and tests only that mock; the production security layer (`crate::sys::security::ToolExecutionGuard`, used by the sibling executor tests) is never invoked.
- **Risk:** Path-traversal, command-injection, and prompt-injection defenses for the desktop AGI executor appear thoroughly tested but the real guard is unverified — the shipped validator can be weaker or broken (or absent) while this suite stays green, giving false security assurance on a trust boundary.
- **Fix:** Point these tests at the real `ToolExecutionGuard`/security validation used in production instead of a local mock, and delete the mock.

### [MEDIUM] assertion theater

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/core/agi/tests/security_tests.rs`
- **Line:** 272-353
- **Instance:** `test_sql_injection_patterns`, `test_dangerous_code_patterns_are_recognized`, and `test_network_request_validation` do not call any validator at all — they assert that the test's own hardcoded attack strings contain `'`/`--`/`os.system`/`http` (e.g. line 283, 333, 351), and line 350 even carries a "Placeholder: Assume validation logic exists" comment.
- **Risk:** These tests can never fail regardless of whether SQL-injection, dangerous-code, or SSRF/internal-IP validation actually exists, masking the absence of those controls.
- **Fix:** Invoke the real validation functions against these inputs and assert the validator rejects them, or remove the tautological assertions.

The security-related instances (`security_tests.rs` whole-file mock, `tool_integration_tests.rs` blocklist copy, `audit_regression_tests.rs` denylist copy) are the highest-impact because they create false assurance on trust-boundary defenses.

## Batch 269 — 20 files scanned

All 20 files are desktop-app Vitest test files (`apps/desktop/src/__tests__/**`). Each was read in full and checked against the taxonomy. Most are conventional mock-driven unit/integration tests with no findings. The findings below capture test-coverage-illusion patterns (tests that exercise inline re-implementations instead of the real production code) and one test that pins a product-rule-violating default.

### [MEDIUM] contract drift

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/__tests__/windows-compat.test.ts`
- **Line:** 215
- **Instance:** The test asserts `state.llmConfig.defaultProvider` equals `'managed_cloud'` as the production default; the production store (`apps/desktop/src/stores/settingsStore.ts:307` and a forced reset at line 1527) really does default to `managed_cloud`.
- **Risk:** v1 is locked LOCAL ONLY with managed cloud waitlist-gated everywhere; a default provider of `managed_cloud` risks silently routing chats to managed cloud across the Local/Managed-Cloud trust boundary, and this passing test locks that default in so the violation looks intentional/correct.
- **Fix:** Confirm the v1 default provider should be a local provider (not `managed_cloud`) per the LOCAL-ONLY lock; update the production store default and this assertion together, or document the gating that prevents silent cloud routing.

### [LOW] coverage illusion

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/__tests__/stream-watchdog.test.ts`
- **Line:** 36
- **Instance:** The file is titled an "E2E Smoke Test" for the stream-end watchdog but tests an inline `createWatchdog(...)` re-implementation (lines 36-70) that "mirrors the actual watchdog pattern" rather than importing the real streaming-hook watchdog code.
- **Risk:** If the production watchdog logic diverges (e.g., the real hook fails to reset `isStreaming`/`currentStreamingMessageId` on timeout), every test still passes, giving false confidence that the watchdog hardening works.
- **Fix:** Import and exercise the real watchdog from the streaming hook/store, or rename the file to make clear it only tests a reference implementation, not the shipped path.

### [LOW] coverage illusion

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/__tests__/updater-interval.test.ts`
- **Line:** 16
- **Instance:** `shouldSkipCheck` is re-implemented inline (lines 16-24) "so it can be tested without rendering the component," instead of importing the real interval-skip logic from `UpdateChecker.tsx`.
- **Risk:** The production interval-skip logic in `UpdateChecker.tsx` could regress (wrong comparison or unit conversion) while this test stays green, masking a real updater bug.
- **Fix:** Extract the skip logic into an exported pure helper and import it in both `UpdateChecker.tsx` and this test so the production code is the thing under test.

### [LOW] hardcoded model id

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/__tests__/tauriMock.test.ts`
- **Line:** 81
- **Instance:** A model id `claude-sonnet-4.6` is hardcoded as the `model` argument for the `llm_send_message` mock invocation (not read from `packages/types/src/models.json`).
- **Risk:** If the canonical model id changes in `models.json`, this literal silently drifts; while it is only a passthrough arg to an echo mock here, hardcoded model ids violate the canonical-catalog rule and can be copy-pasted into non-test code.
- **Fix:** Reference a model id from the canonical `models.json` catalog (or a shared test fixture derived from it) instead of a string literal.

### [MEDIUM] coverage illusion / test theater

- **Instance:** The suite defines a private local `ScrollToBottomButton` component ("mirroring ChatStream.tsx lines 928-944") and tests that copy instead of importing the real button from `ChatStream.tsx`; the production component is never rendered or asserted against.
- **Risk:** The real scroll-to-bottom control in ChatStream can regress (wrong aria-label, broken visibility/onClick, removed entirely) while this suite stays green, giving false confidence that the feature is covered.
- **Fix:** Extract the button into its own importable component (or export it from ChatStream) and render that real component in the test rather than a hand-copied duplicate.

### [MEDIUM] coverage illusion / test theater

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/__tests__/Sidebar.test.tsx`
- **Line:** 9-36
- **Instance:** `getTemporalGroup` is re-implemented inline in the test file and all temporal-grouping assertions run against this local copy, not against the Sidebar component's real grouping function.
- **Risk:** A bug introduced in the Sidebar's actual `getTemporalGroup`/grouping logic will not be caught — the test validates a fork of the logic that can silently drift out of sync with production.
- **Fix:** Export `getTemporalGroup` from the Sidebar source module and import it here so the test exercises the real implementation.

### [MEDIUM] coverage illusion / test theater

- **Fix:** Remove the no-op `vi.mock` for `../ToolLabel` and let the real module load normally.

### [LOW] inconsistent imports

- **Line:** 39
- **Instance:** `vi.fn()` is used but `vi` is not imported on line 1 (only `describe, expect, it`); it resolves only because `globals: true` is set in `apps/desktop/vite.config.ts` (line 363).

## Batch 271 — 20 files scanned

All 20 files are desktop-surface (`apps/desktop`) Vitest test files (`.test.ts` / `.test.tsx`). Each was read in full and checked against the testing, AI-code-quality, and security failure modes in the taxonomy. Findings below; clean files listed at the bottom.

### [HIGH] test theater

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/memory/__tests__/MemoryManager.test.ts`
- **Line:** 7-349
- **Instance:** The suite is named `MemoryManager` and a real `MemoryManager.tsx` component exists in the same feature dir, but the test never imports or renders that component — every `it()` block re-implements `.filter()`/`.sort()`/`.includes()` logic on locally-declared `mockMemories` arrays and asserts on its own inline re-implementation (e.g. lines 42-44, 78-82, 154-159, 335-347).
- **Risk:** The component's real filtering, sorting, search, export, and category-count code paths are completely untested while CI reports green "MemoryManager" coverage, so a regression in the actual component ships undetected.
- **Fix:** Import and render `MemoryManager` (or its store-backed selectors) and assert against the rendered output / store mutations rather than testing standalone array literals.

### [LOW] mock-only test

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/memory/__tests__/MemoryManager.test.ts`
- **Line:** 226-279
- **Instance:** The "export functionality" tests build a plain `exportData` object literal in the test and assert `JSON.stringify`/`JSON.parse` round-trips it, exercising only the JS runtime, not any export helper from the component.
- **Risk:** Gives a false sense that the export feature is covered; the real export code (filename, blob, download trigger, filter snapshot) is unverified.
- **Fix:** Call the component's actual export function and assert on the emitted payload/filename.

### [LOW] test deletion

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/research/__tests__/ResearchPanel.test.tsx`
- **Line:** 79
- **Instance:** The "shows mode selector with all options" test is permanently `it.skip(...)` with a comment that the Radix Select portal does not render in jsdom, leaving the mode-selector (Quick/Standard/Deep/Exhaustive) interaction unverified.
- **Risk:** A regression in the research-mode dropdown wiring would not be caught; the skipped block can also silently rot out of sync with the component.
- **Fix:** Replace with a userEvent/portal-aware assertion or a lightweight Radix Select mock (as `MessageHistory.test.tsx` does) instead of skipping indefinitely.

### [LOW] coverage illusion

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/screen-capture/RegionSelector.test.tsx`
- **Line:** 5-16
- **Instance:** The only test for `RegionSelector` asserts it mounts into a `document.body` portal and shows static helper text; the core drag-to-select interaction (mousedown/move/up → region rect → `onConfirm` payload) is never exercised, and neither `onConfirm` nor `onCancel` is ever asserted to fire.
- **Risk:** The component's actual selection logic and callback contract ship unverified behind a passing test, masking selection/coordinate regressions.
- **Fix:** Add interaction tests that simulate a drag and assert the computed region passed to `onConfirm`, plus an Escape/cancel path that calls `onCancel`.

### [LOW] magic constants

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/__tests__/UnifiedAgenticChat.test.tsx`
- **Line:** 154, 327-330, 360
- **Instance:** Test mocks hardcode model IDs (`gpt-5.5`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`) and assert `modelOverride: 'gpt-5.5'` (line 730) rather than reading from the canonical `packages/types/src/models.json`; these literals will silently drift if the canonical catalog is renamed.
- **Risk:** A model-ID rename in `models.json` leaves these tests asserting on a stale ID, masking a real routing break in `chat_send_message`; this is fixture-only (not a production model-ID source-of-truth violation).
- **Fix:** Reference model IDs from the shared catalog/constants in the test, or document that these are intentionally inert fixture strings.

## Batch 280 — 20 files scanned

All 20 files in this batch are Jest/Vitest test files and Jest mock stubs for the mobile and Chrome-extension surfaces. They were read line-by-line in full. No secrets, PII, prompt leakage, or trust-boundary violations were found. The few findings below are test-hygiene / drift risks (LOW–MEDIUM). Notably, several files in this batch actively and correctly pin the LOCAL/BYOK/Managed-Cloud trust boundary (e.g. `chatStore.test.ts` asserts locked cloud models do NOT fall back to local generation, and local models stay on-device even when remote chat is allowed), and `biometric-gate.test.tsx` pins fail-closed biometric behavior — these are positive controls, not findings.

### [MEDIUM] test drift / coverage illusion

- **File:** `apps/mobile/__tests__/chat-tab-greeting.snapshot.test.tsx`
- **Line:** 12
- **Instance:** The test re-implements `getTimeOfDayGreeting()` inline ("mirrors the one in chat.tsx") instead of importing the production function, so it tests its own copy of the logic, not the shipped code.
- **Risk:** If the real greeting thresholds/strings in `chat.tsx` drift (e.g. boundary hours change), this test stays green and the regression ships unnoticed — a false sense of coverage.
- **Fix:** Export the greeting helper from the production module and import it here so the test exercises the actual shipped logic.

### [LOW] hardcoded model id

- **File:** `apps/mobile/__tests__/chatStore.test.ts`
- **Line:** 167
- **Instance:** `const MODEL = 'claude-3-5-sonnet';` hardcodes a model ID directly in the test rather than referencing `packages/types/src/models.json` (the canonical source).
- **Risk:** If that model ID is renamed/retired in the canonical catalog, the test continues using a stale literal and drifts from the real model registry.
- **Fix:** Derive the test model id from the canonical models catalog or a shared test fixture instead of a bare string literal.

### [LOW] hardcoded model id

- **File:** `apps/mobile/__tests__/chatStore.test.ts`
- **Line:** 169
- **Instance:** `const CLOUD_MODEL = LOCKED_CLOUD_MODELS[0]?.id ?? 'gpt-5.5';` uses a hardcoded `'gpt-5.5'` fallback model ID when `LOCKED_CLOUD_MODELS` is empty.
- **Risk:** If `LOCKED_CLOUD_MODELS` is ever empty, the cloud-routing assertions silently run against a fabricated model id (`gpt-5.5`) that may not exist in the canonical catalog, weakening the trust-boundary assertions.
- **Fix:** Make the fallback fail loudly (throw/skip) rather than substituting an invented model id, or pull the fixture from the canonical catalog.

### [LOW] hardcoded model id

- **File:** `apps/mobile/__tests__/chat-input.test.tsx`
- **Line:** 151
- **Instance:** The `useModelStore` mock hardcodes `selectedModel: 'claude-sonnet-4.6'` (and the `getShortDisplayName` mock at line 158 maps that literal), unconnected to the canonical model catalog.
- **Risk:** Drift from the canonical model registry; the test asserts a display name for a literal id that may diverge from the shipped catalog.
- **Fix:** Reference a canonical model id constant/fixture in the mock rather than a bare string literal.

### [LOW] documentation/contract ambiguity

- **File:** `apps/mobile/__tests__/biometric-flag-store.test.ts`
- **Line:** 4
- **Instance:** The file header comment says the in-memory flag "defaults to ENABLED until hydration completes," but the tested contract (lines 51–56) is that a never-set/`null` value resolves to `enabled=false` after hydration so first-run users are not locked out; the header's wording can mislead future readers about the fail-open-vs-fail-closed boundary.
- **Risk:** A future maintainer trusting the header could "fix" the null-handling toward fail-closed and lock out all first-run users, or vice versa weaken the SecureStore-error fail-closed path.
- **Fix:** Tighten the header comment to state precisely: SecureStore read error → fail-closed (enabled=true); absent/`null` persisted value → enabled=false (first-run not locked).

## Batch 283 — 20 files scanned

### [MEDIUM] flaky test

- **File:** `apps/mobile/__tests__/notification-auth-gate.test.ts`
- **Line:** 113
- **Instance:** `jest.useFakeTimers()` is enabled AFTER `fireNotification()` already ran synchronously, so any setTimeout-deferred `safeNavigate` scheduled during the fire was registered against real timers; `advanceTimersByTime(200)` then operates on a fresh fake clock that never holds those callbacks.
- **Risk:** The "routes to login when no session" assertion can pass for the wrong reason (immediate path) or flake if the deferred path is taken, giving false confidence in the auth-gate regression coverage.
- **Fix:** Call `jest.useFakeTimers()` in a `beforeEach` before firing the notification, fire inside `act`, then advance timers.

### [LOW] assertion theater

- **File:** `apps/mobile/__tests__/paywall-bottom-sheet.test.tsx`
- **Line:** 205
- **Instance:** The test titled "calls onDismiss when 'Try later' is pressed" asserts `expect(onDismiss).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` and only confirms the press does not throw, so the test name contradicts its assertion and the dismiss path (via mocked BottomSheet.onChange) is never actually exercised.
- **Risk:** A regression that breaks the "Try later" dismiss flow would not be caught; the green test misleads maintainers into thinking dismiss is covered.
- **Fix:** Either rename the test to reflect that it only verifies no-throw, or mock the sheet ref/onChange path so the actual onDismiss invocation can be asserted.

## Batch 286 — 20 files scanned

All 20 files are Vitest API-route test suites under `apps/web/__tests__/api/`. Per the taxonomy, tests are scanned for test theater, assertion theater, false-green/weak assertions, mock leakage, and drift. The production routes they exercise are not in this batch and were not modified (read-only). Findings below cite real lines read in these test files.

### [LOW] no-op logic / dead branch

- **File:** `apps/web/__tests__/api/device-link.test.ts`
- **Line:** 47
- **Instance:** The `requireEnv` mock has two consecutive `if (key === 'NEON_DATABASE_URL')` branches (lines 47 and 48); the second (`return 'test-service-role-key'`) is unreachable dead code, and the env key meant for the Clerk secret is mislabeled.
- **Risk:** Test mock drifts from the real route's env contract, so a future regression where the route reads a distinct DB-vs-secret env var would not be caught.
- **Fix:** Collapse the duplicate branches and map each distinct env key (NEON_DATABASE_URL, CLERK_SECRET_KEY) to its own return value.

### [LOW] no-op logic / dead branch

- **File:** `apps/web/__tests__/api/device-poll.test.ts`
- **Line:** 31
- **Instance:** The `requireEnv` mock contains three identical `if (key === 'NEON_DATABASE_URL')` branches (lines 31-33) with conflicting return values (`'https://localhost'`, `'https://localhost'`, `'test-service-role-key'`); only the first is reachable, the others are dead code.
- **Risk:** Mock confusion obscures what env values the route actually depends on; copy-paste residue can mask a real env-validation gap in the route under test.
- **Fix:** Reduce to one branch per distinct env key with the correct intended value.

### [MEDIUM] false-green test / misleading assertion

- **File:** `apps/web/__tests__/api/llm-completion.test.ts`
- **Line:** 537
- **Instance:** The test "should return 402 when the billing-period usage budget is exhausted" mocks `CreditService.deductCredits` to return `code: 'DAILY_CREDIT_LIMIT_REACHED'` (line 506) but then asserts the response `data.code` equals `'MONTHLY_CREDIT_LIMIT_REACHED'` (line 537), so the assertion does not match the mocked input code.
- **Risk:** If the route ever stops remapping the daily code to monthly (or the mapping is wrong), this test could still pass for the wrong reason or hide a contract drift between the credit-service code and the user-facing error code.
- **Fix:** Assert against the actual code the route is expected to emit and add an explicit comment/assertion documenting the daily→monthly remap, or assert the original `DAILY_CREDIT_LIMIT_REACHED` if no remap is intended.

### [MEDIUM] assertion theater

- **File:** `apps/web/__tests__/api/memory.test.ts`
- **Line:** 391
- **Instance:** The test "should trim content and category before saving" claims to verify trimming but only asserts `expect(mockQuery).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` (line 404) and never checks that the trimmed values (`'Trimmed content'`, `'health'`) were actually passed to the query.
- **Risk:** A regression that stops trimming (storing `'  Trimmed content  '`) would still pass this test, so the trimming behavior is effectively untested despite the test name asserting coverage.
- **Fix:** Assert `mockQuery` was called with the trimmed args, e.g. `expect.arrayContaining(['Trimmed content', 'health'])`.

### [LOW] fail-open behavior (documented in test)

- **File:** `apps/web/__tests__/api/routing-preferences.test.ts`
- **Line:** 121
- **Instance:** The test "returns empty object on DB error (fail-open)" asserts that GET returns 200 + `{}` when the Neon query rejects (lines 121-127), locking in fail-open behavior for the routing-preferences read path.
- **Risk:** Fail-open on a DB error silently serves default (non-US-only) routing preferences; a user who set `us_only: true` could be transparently routed to a non-US provider during a DB outage without any error surfaced — a routing/geo-preference correctness risk for a privacy-sensitive control.
- **Fix:** Confirm with product that silently defaulting geo-routing preferences on DB error is acceptable; if not, surface a degraded/error state so callers do not assume defaults are the user's choice (track as a route-level decision, this finding flags the locked-in behavior).

### [LOW] weak negative assertion

- **File:** `apps/web/__tests__/api/csrf.test.ts`
- **Line:** 202
- **Instance:** The "proceeds normally with valid CSRF token" cases assert only `expect(response.status).not.toBe(403)` (lines 202, 233, 277, 307), which passes for any non-403 status including 500s, rather than asserting the expected success status.
- **Risk:** A route that crashes (500) after passing CSRF would still satisfy these tests, giving a false sense that the happy path works.
- **Fix:** Assert the concrete expected success status (200/201) in addition to the explicit `requireCsrfToken` call-count assertion that already accompanies these cases.

## Batch 288 — 20 files scanned

Scope note: 19 of 20 files are vitest/jsdom test files (`*.test.ts` / `*.test.tsx`). Per taxonomy these were reviewed for test-quality failure modes (assertion theater, coverage illusion, mock-only/false-green, snapshot abuse) and for secrets/PII. Only one file is production code: `apps/web/app/api/messaging/test/[platform]/route.ts`, which received full semantic review. Model-like identifiers (`claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, `gpt-5.5`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`) appear only inside vitest mock factories / SSE fixtures, not as production model resolution, so they are NOT model-ID-hardcoding findings.

### [MEDIUM] implementation theater

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/messaging/test/[platform]/route.ts`
- **Line:** 93
- **Instance:** The route documented as "Test connection to a messaging platform" never attempts any connection — it only checks that a single config field (phone/token/workspaceUrl) is a non-empty string, then returns `{ success: true }`.
- **Risk:** Users clicking "Test connection" get a green success result for credentials that are wrong/expired/unreachable, so broken WhatsApp/Telegram/Slack integrations silently appear healthy until a real message fails.
- **Fix:** Either perform a real lightweight liveness probe to the platform API, or rename the endpoint/response to "validate config shape" so the success signal does not overstate what was verified.

### [LOW] hardcoded success

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/messaging/test/[platform]/route.ts`
- **Line:** 95
- **Instance:** `return NextResponse.json({ success: true })` is returned unconditionally whenever `validatePlatformConfig` passes, with a comment deferring the real connection test to "a future phase."
- **Risk:** The hardcoded success path is indistinguishable from a real connectivity check in the response contract, masking the stub for any client consuming `success`.
- **Fix:** Add a `validatedOnly: true` (or similar) flag to the response so callers can distinguish shape-validation from an actual connection test.

### [LOW] coverage illusion

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/auth/desktop-token/__tests__/keysource-entropy.test.ts`
- **Line:** 36
- **Instance:** The test imports `../route` only to `void mod` (line 38) and then re-implements the entropy/scrypt assertion logic inline (lines 39-59) instead of invoking the route's real `getEncryptionKey`, as the file's own comment admits ("we can't easily invoke the route handler here, we simulate the same pattern").
- **Risk:** The entropy gate in the production route could be removed or weakened and these tests would still pass, because they validate a copy of the logic rather than the shipped code.
- **Fix:** Export `getEncryptionKey` (or a testable wrapper) from the route module and assert against it directly so the gate is actually under test.

### [LOW] assertion theater

- **File:** `apps/web/app/__tests__/dark-mode-colors.test.ts`
- **Line:** 163
- **Instance:** The test "white/7% opacity is rgba(255,255,255,0.07)" builds the rgba string from the literal `0.07` and then asserts it equals `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.07)` — it tests JS string interpolation, not any application token or CSS value.
- **Risk:** This test can never fail for a real regression in the design token; it gives false confidence that border opacity is verified.
- **Fix:** Assert the opacity value as actually read from `globals.css` / the Tailwind config, or delete the tautological assertion.

### [LOW] type erasure

- **File:** `apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/__tests__/stream-transform-usage.test.ts`
- **Line:** 55
- **Instance:** Multiple `as any` casts are used for the `chatRequest`, `quotaFeature`, and `makeRequest()`/`makeStream()` arguments to `buildStreamResponse` (lines 55, 60, 71, 125, 132, etc.), erasing the function's input types in the test harness.
- **Risk:** A contract/type drift in `ProcessedRequest` or `buildStreamResponse`'s signature would not be caught by these tests because the casts suppress the type checker at the call boundary.
- **Fix:** Build properly-typed stubs (or a typed factory returning the real interface) so a signature change forces a compile error in the test.

## Batch 290 — 20 files scanned

All 20 files in this batch are test (`.test.ts` / `.test.tsx`) and Playwright e2e spec (`.spec.ts`) files. They were reviewed line-by-line for test theater, false-green/coverage-illusion patterns, snapshot abuse, hardcoded model-ID drift, and leaked secrets/PII in fixtures.

### [MEDIUM] test drift / coverage illusion

- **File:** `apps/web/core/security/api-abuse-prevention.test.ts`
- **Line:** 366-405
- **Instance:** The "Model cost tier detection" suite asserts cost-tier categorization for model IDs that no longer exist in the canonical catalog (`claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, `claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022`, `gemini-1.5-pro`, `gemini-2.0-flash`, `grok-2`, `o1-mini`, `sonar-reasoning`); verified these are absent from `packages/types/src/models.json` while production `getModelCostTier` looks them up via `getModelMetadataById` first (api-abuse-prevention.ts:74), so they silently fall through to the lowercase-substring fallback heuristic.
- **Risk:** The tests named "should categorize high/medium/low-cost models correctly" only assert `result.allowed === true` (always true on a first request regardless of tier), so they never verify the tier mapping they claim to test — masking real drift in the cost-tier classifier that gates abuse throttling.
- **Fix:** Replace the stale model IDs with current catalog IDs from `packages/types/src/models.json` and assert the resolved tier (e.g., via per-minute limit behavior) rather than only `allowed`.

### [LOW] test drift / hardcoded model IDs

- **File:** `apps/web/core/integrations/token-usage-tracker.test.ts`
- **Line:** 10-15
- **Instance:** Provider-default model IDs are hardcoded as bare string constants (`gpt-5.5`, `claude-sonnet-4.6`, `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, `sonar-pro`, `grok-4.3`, `claude-haiku-4.5`) at the top of the file rather than read from the canonical accessor; the cost-assertion helper does correctly call `getModelMetadataById`, but the IDs themselves are literals.
- **Risk:** If a model is renamed or removed from `packages/types/src/models.json`, these tests pass against stale identifiers (cost helper falls back to a $1/1M default), giving false confidence instead of failing loudly.
- **Fix:** Source the model IDs from a canonical helper (e.g., `requireProviderDefaultModel(provider)`) so a catalog change forces a test update, matching the pattern already used in `web-search-handler.test.ts:185`.

### [LOW] test drift / hardcoded model IDs

- **File:** `apps/web/core/integrations/chat-completion-handler.test.ts`
- **Line:** 60, 82, 132, 141
- **Instance:** Test fixtures hardcode model-ID string literals (`gpt-5.5`, `claude-haiku-4.5`) directly in mock responses and call arguments instead of referencing the `DEFAULT_*_MODEL` constants already imported at the top of the file.
- **Risk:** Mixed literal/constant usage makes the suite resistant to catalog renames; literal IDs continue to pass even after the canonical catalog drops them.
- **Fix:** Use the imported `DEFAULT_OPENAI_MODEL` / collaboration-model constants for the custom-model cases, keeping all model references catalog-derived.

### [MEDIUM] mock-only test / coverage illusion

- **File:** `apps/web/features/chat/components/__tests__/InlineToolResult.test.tsx`

- **Instance:** The test `vi.mock('../InlineToolResults', ...)` replaces the entire module under test with an inline reimplementation of `getToolRenderer` and `InlineToolResult`, so every assertion exercises the test's own stub rather than the production component.
- **Risk:** The real `InlineToolResults` registry, lazy-loading, and `web-search-results` type override could regress (or never have worked) while this suite stays green, producing false confidence and zero real coverage of the file it claims to test.
- **Fix:** Mock only the heavy lazy sub-components (e.g. `InlineSearchResults`) and import the real `InlineToolResult`/`getToolRenderer` so the production registry logic is actually executed.

- **Line:** 56-66, 96-106, 140-143
- **Instance:** Tests assert on hardcoded Tailwind utility class names (`bg-terra-cotta-500`, `bg-muted`, `bg-red-500`, `shadow-red-500/25`, `bg-amber-500`) as a proxy for visual state rather than testing behavior.
- **Risk:** A pure styling refactor (renaming a token or moving to a CSS variable) breaks the suite even though behavior is unchanged, creating maintenance churn and discouraging refactors.
- **Fix:** Assert on stable semantic hooks (aria-label/title/data-state) for state, leaving exact class names to visual/snapshot tooling.

- **File:** `apps/web/features/settings/hooks/use-settings-queries-wiring.test.ts`

- **Risk:** These tests would stay green even if the hook's fetch wiring regressed, because the production hook is never executed in these blocks; the title implies hook coverage that does not exist, masking real wiring drift.
- **Fix:** Invoke the actual hook via renderHook (as the sibling `use-settings-queries-renderhook.test.tsx` does) and assert on `result.current`, or remove the hand-rolled fetch blocks and rely only on the `.toString()` anti-stub guards plus the renderHook test.

- **Risk:** Low — the test never asserts on the model field (only URL/method/headers), so it cannot fail on drift, but the literal can rot silently and become misleading if the canonical haiku id changes.

## Batch 293 — 20 files scanned

All 20 files in this batch are Vitest test suites for the web app's security, quota, pricing, and AI-SDK libraries. They are generally well-constructed, exercising real security boundaries (SSRF egress policy, CSRF rotation, safe-redirect, managed/BYOK/Local trust-boundary gates, quota caps). The findings below are the few cases where a test enshrines a fail-open or weak-guard design in the source under test, plus minor robustness notes.

### [MEDIUM] fail-open behavior

- **File:** `apps/web/lib/__tests__/assert-quota.test.ts`
- **Line:** 323
- **Instance:** The test `returns ok when DB error fetching usage row (fail-open)` asserts that when the usage-row query rejects, `assertQuota` assumes 0 tokens used and returns `kind: 'ok'`, allowing the request through.
- **Risk:** During a Neon DB outage or transient query failure, the quota/billing gate stops metering and every tier (including Free) can bypass the token cap, enabling unmetered/free compute and cost leakage on managed cloud.
- **Fix:** Change the source (`lib/assert-quota.ts`) and this test to fail-closed (or degrade to a conservative cached/last-known usage) on DB error rather than assuming zero usage; at minimum emit an alert and a short-lived hard limit.

### [LOW] fail-open behavior

- **File:** `apps/web/lib/__tests__/assert-quota.test.ts`
- **Line:** 653
- **Instance:** The test `does not throw when execute fails (fire-and-forget semantics)` pins `reconcileUsage` to swallow `increment_usage` RPC failures silently (`resolves.toBeUndefined()`), so usage that fails to persist is never retried or surfaced.
- **Risk:** Repeated RPC failures cause systematic under-counting of consumed tokens; users could exceed caps indefinitely because reconciliation never records the spend, and there is no compensating queue or alert.
- **Fix:** Capture reconcile failures into a durable retry/dead-letter path or at least increment an error metric so silent metering loss is observable.

### [LOW] entropy check is byte-length only

- **File:** `apps/web/lib/__tests__/csrf-rotation.test.ts`
- **Line:** 108
- **Instance:** The test `repeated-character secret still passes if length >= 32` confirms the CSRF secret guard accepts `'a'.repeat(38)` — a fully low-entropy HMAC key passes the startup check.
- **Risk:** An operator who sets a long-but-trivial `CSRF_SECRET` (e.g. all-same-char) gets no warning; a guessable HMAC key weakens CSRF token forgeability protection.
- **Fix:** Mirror the stricter `assertHighEntropyKeysource()` heuristic (reject repeated/low-distinct-char secrets) in the CSRF secret validator, as the comment itself acknowledges the gap.

### [LOW] dead/over-permissive test assertion (host allowlist)

- **File:** `apps/web/lib/__tests__/safe-redirect.test.ts`
- **Line:** 52
- **Instance:** The test `allows allowed hosts` asserts `https://chat.agiworkforce.com/room/123` is accepted and rewritten to a relative path, confirming the source allows cross-subdomain redirect targets beyond the request origin.
- **Risk:** Any subdomain added to the allowlist (or a future takeover of `chat.agiworkforce.com`) becomes a valid open-redirect target; the allowlist is an implicit trust expansion that is easy to overlook.
- **Fix:** Ensure the source allowlist is a tightly curated constant with a comment justifying each host, and add a negative test for a non-allowlisted same-parent-domain host to lock the boundary.

## Batch 294 — 20 files scanned

### [MEDIUM] test theater

- **File:** `apps/web/shared/hooks/useSessionTimeout.test.ts`
- **Line:** 7-10, 129-131, 177-181, 192-193, 208-216
- **Instance:** The test file never imports or invokes the real `useSessionTimeout` hook or its `SessionTimeoutWarning` component; instead it re-declares the timeout constants, throttle predicate, time-format function, critical-state predicate, and activity-event list inline and asserts against those local copies.
- **Risk:** The suite stays green even if the actual hook implementation is deleted, broken, or diverges from these inline copies (coverage illusion) — a real session-timeout regression would not be caught.
- **Fix:** Import the actual constants/helpers and render the real hook with `renderHook`, asserting on its observable behavior rather than re-implemented logic.

### [LOW] assertion theater

- **File:** `apps/web/services/__tests__/download.test.ts`
- **Line:** 148-156
- **Instance:** The `showErrorToast` test does not call `showErrorToast` at all; its comment admits "we'll just verify the error has the right structure" and only asserts `error.message === 'Test error'`, which the test itself constructed.
- **Risk:** The named function is never exercised, so any defect in `showErrorToast` (e.g., not invoking the toast library, wrong message mapping) ships undetected.
- **Fix:** Either spy on the `sonner` toast module and assert it was called with the expected payload, or remove the placeholder test.

### [LOW] test drift

- **File:** `apps/web/shared/components/__tests__/theme-contrast.test.ts`
- **Line:** 74-95
- **Instance:** WCAG contrast assertions are computed from HSL/hex color literals copied by hand from `globals.css` (e.g. `--background: 40 23% 97%`, `#faf9f7`, `#0f0f13`) rather than parsed from the source CSS.
- **Risk:** If `globals.css` token values change, these literals can silently drift out of sync, so the test would validate stale colors and give a false-green accessibility signal.
- **Fix:** Parse the actual CSS-variable values from `globals.css` at test time (or import a shared tokens module) so the contrast math always reflects the shipped palette.

### [LOW] environment validation gap

- **File:** `apps/web/playwright.config.ts`
- **Line:** 14-25
- **Instance:** A hand-rolled `.env.local` parser splits each line on `=`, strips quotes, and writes every key/value directly into `process.env`, with no validation, type coercion, or guard against overwriting already-set process env vars.
- **Risk:** Malformed lines or stray `=` characters are silently mis-parsed, and existing process env values are unconditionally overwritten by file contents, which can mask CI-provided config during local-vs-CI runs.
- **Fix:** Use a maintained loader such as `dotenv` (with `override: false`) instead of the bespoke parser, or guard against clobbering pre-set env vars.

## Batch 295 — 20 files scanned

### [LOW] flaky test

- **File:** `apps/web/shared/stores/mission-control-store.test.ts`
- **Line:** 533
- **Instance:** Test asserts `expect(end - start).toBeLessThan(100)` using wall-clock `performance.now()` to gate setting a 1000-task plan.
- **Risk:** Wall-clock timing assertions flake under CI load / slow runners, producing intermittent false-red builds unrelated to correctness.
- **Fix:** Remove the timing assertion (it tests environment speed, not store logic) or replace with a generous, non-load-sensitive budget behind an explicit perf-test flag.

### [LOW] flaky test

- **File:** `apps/web/shared/stores/mission-control-store.test.ts`
- **Line:** 546
- **Instance:** Test asserts `expect(end - start).toBeLessThan(100)` over a 100-iteration `performance.now()` measurement of employee updates.
- **Risk:** Same wall-clock timing fragility as line 533 — intermittent CI flakes when the runner is under contention.
- **Fix:** Drop the wall-clock timing assertion; keep only the functional `Object.keys(...).length` check.

### [MEDIUM] edge-case blindness

- **File:** `apps/web/shared/stores/usage-warning-store.test.ts`
- **Line:** 253
- **Instance:** Test asserts `usagePercentage` equals `Infinity` when `updateUsage(1000, 0)` is called with a zero limit (comment on line 248 confirms "would cause division by zero without protection"), codifying that the production store performs unguarded division by `totalLimit`.
- **Risk:** A zero/undefined token limit yields `Infinity` for the usage percentage, which propagates to UI/progress rendering (NaN/Infinity width, broken warning gates) instead of being clamped or treated as an error state.
- **Fix:** Guard the percentage computation in the production store (e.g. return 0 or a defined max when `totalLimit <= 0`) and update this test to assert the clamped value rather than locking in `Infinity`.

### [LOW] flaky test

- **File:** `apps/web/shared/stores/workforce-store.test.ts`
- **Line:** 505
- **Instance:** Performance test asserts `expect(end - start).toBeLessThan(100)` using wall-clock `performance.now()` around an async fetch of 100 employees.
- **Risk:** Wall-clock timing assertion can flake under CI contention, async scheduling jitter, or slow runners, causing false-red builds.
- **Fix:** Remove the timing assertion (it does not test store correctness) or gate it behind an explicit, generously-budgeted perf suite.

### [LOW] assertion theater

- **File:** `apps/web/shared/ui/__tests__/theme-toggle.test.tsx`
- **Line:** 63
- **Instance:** Test named "renders an icon for each theme state" re-renders with system/light/dark themes but only asserts `screen.getByRole('button')` is in the document each time; it never verifies the rendered icon actually differs per theme.
- **Risk:** A regression where the wrong icon (or no icon) renders for a theme would pass this test, giving false confidence in icon-per-state coverage.
- **Fix:** Assert on the actual icon (e.g. a `data-testid` or accessible name) for each theme state rather than only the button's presence.

### [LOW] spec mismatch

- **File:** `apps/web/shared/ui/button.test.tsx`
- **Line:** 123
- **Instance:** Test asserts `size="sm"` yields class `h-10`, identical to the `size="default"` height asserted on line 117, so the "small" size renders the same height as default.
- **Risk:** If a distinct small button height was intended, this size variant is a no-op visually and the test silently locks in the collision; if intentional, the variant is redundant.
- **Fix:** Confirm the intended `sm` height against the design tokens in `button.tsx`; if `sm` should be shorter, fix the variant and update the assertion.

- **File:** `crates/agiworkforce-command-registry/tests/slash_palette_golden.rs`

- **Instance:** A checked-in doc-comment hardcodes the maintainer's absolute home path `/Users/siddhartha/Desktop/reference/ui-capture-runs/...` as the golden calibration source.
- **Risk:** Leaks the developer username/local filesystem layout in committed source, and the reference is unresolvable on any other machine so the provenance note rots.

### [LOW] flaky test

- **File:** `crates/agiworkforce-task-runtime/tests/lifecycle.rs`
- **Line:** 186
- **Instance:** `test_watchdog_aborts_on_drop` asserts `matches!(task.status, TaskStatus::Running | TaskStatus::Failed)`, accepting BOTH outcomes, with an in-comment admission of a 200ms-vs-0ms timing race.
- **Risk:** The test passes regardless of whether the watchdog abort-on-drop actually works, so a real regression where the dropped watchdog still fires would go undetected (assertion theater / coverage illusion).
- **Fix:** Make the drop deterministic (e.g. assert the spawned task handle is aborted, or use a controllable clock / longer timeout) so the test fails when abort-on-drop regresses.

## Batch 297 — 20 files scanned

All 20 files are vitest/unit test suites under `packages/*/src/__tests__/`. Read line-by-line in full. They are generally high quality: several encode real security behavior (JWT default-deny RLS binding, profile-name path-traversal validation, fail-closed Chinese-HQ provider gate, Article 50 disclosure gate that blocks outbound traffic before consent). Findings below are limited to test-fixture hygiene/drift; no exploitable defects were found in the test code itself.

### [LOW] hardcoded model ID

- **File:** `packages/llm-runtime/src/__tests__/errors.test.ts`
- **Line:** 211
- **Instance:** `FallbackTriggeredError('claude-opus-4.8', 'claude-sonnet-4.6', ...)` hardcodes two model IDs as test fixtures rather than sourcing them from `@agiworkforce/types` models.json.
- **Risk:** If these IDs are renamed/retired in the canonical catalog, the test keeps passing against stale strings, masking model-catalog drift; inconsistent with the locked "never hardcode model IDs" rule that the sibling `fallback.test.ts` explicitly honors.
- **Fix:** Use opaque placeholder strings (e.g. `'model-a'`/`'model-b'`) or pull real IDs from `getModelsForProvider('anthropic')` like `fallback.test.ts` does.

### [LOW] hardcoded model ID

- **File:** `packages/compliance/src/__tests__/article50-marker.test.ts`
- **Line:** 39
- **Instance:** `buildProvenanceClaim({ ... model: 'claude-opus-4.8' ... })` plus `imagen-4-fast` (line 17), `gpt-image-1` (line 53), and `claude-haiku-4.5` (lines 82, 91, 112) are hardcoded model IDs used as provenance-claim fixtures.
- **Risk:** Test fixtures encode invented/stale model IDs that can drift from the canonical `models.json`, and `claude-opus-4.8` does not match the host runtime model id `claude-opus-4-8` (dash vs dot form) used elsewhere, risking confusion if anyone treats these as canonical.
- **Fix:** Replace with neutral fixture strings (e.g. `'test-model'`) since the marker logic only treats `model` as an opaque label, or derive from the catalog.

### [LOW] hardcoded model ID

- **File:** `packages/compliance/src/__tests__/llm-gate.integration.test.ts`
- **Line:** 91
- **Instance:** Model IDs `claude-haiku-4.5` (lines 91, 121) and `deepseek-v4-flash` (lines 154, 182) are hardcoded as `send()` fixtures rather than sourced from the canonical catalog.
- **Risk:** Hardcoded/invented model IDs in tests can drift from `models.json`; `deepseek-v4-flash` may not exist in the catalog, so the fixture asserts behavior against a model the product may never expose.
- **Fix:** Use opaque model placeholder strings since the gate keys on `providerId`, not on the specific model id.

### [LOW] hardcoded model ID

- **File:** `packages/llm-normalize/src/__tests__/openai-reasoning-effort.test.ts`
- **Line:** 23
- **Instance:** The whole suite pins concrete OpenAI model IDs (`gpt-5.4-mini`, `gpt-5`, `gpt-5.1`, `gpt-5.2`, `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.5-pro`, `gpt-5.1-codex-max`, `gpt-5.1-codex-mini`, lines 23-103) directly in assertions.
- **Risk:** These golden tests intentionally pin family-inference behavior, but the IDs are not cross-checked against `models.json`, so a catalog rename leaves the effort-resolution mapping untested for the real id while the test stays green (coverage illusion / catalog drift).

## Batch 298 — 20 files scanned

### [MEDIUM] assertion theater

- **File:** `packages/llm-runtime/src/__tests__/retry.test.ts`
- **Line:** 286
- **Instance:** The test titled "does not invoke onEvent if hook throws (does not catch)" never calls `withRetry` or any production code — its body only constructs `const hook = vi.fn()` and asserts `expect(hook).not.toBeCalled()`, which is trivially true and verifies nothing about the documented onEvent-throws-propagation contract.
- **Risk:** A real regression where a throwing `onEvent` hook is silently swallowed by `withRetry` would never be caught, giving false confidence that the error-propagation contract is tested.
- **Fix:** Replace the no-op body with a real exercise: pass an `onEvent` that throws to `withRetry` and assert the thrown error propagates (e.g. `await expect(withRetry(...,{onEvent: throwingHook})).rejects.toThrow()`), or delete the misleading test.

### [MEDIUM] coverage illusion

- **File:** `packages/llm-runtime/src/__tests__/retry.test.ts`
- **Line:** 204
- **Instance:** The "property test: 100 simulated failure paths" picks errors with unseeded `Math.random()` (line 239) but its only assertion is `expect(successes + cannots + fallbacks).toBe(100)` (line 266) — a tautology that holds whenever every iteration reaches a terminal branch without rethrowing, even if all 100 runs take a single path; the comment's promise to verify "at least some of each terminal class" is never asserted.
- **Risk:** A classification regression that collapses every error to one outcome (e.g. always CannotRetryError) still passes, and the unseeded RNG makes the run non-deterministic so a genuinely-unexpected throw appears only flakily.
- **Fix:** Seed the RNG (or iterate deterministically over `fakeErrors`) and assert each terminal class is reached for the inputs that should produce it (e.g. `expect(fallbacks).toBeGreaterThan(0)` and `expect(cannots).toBeGreaterThan(0)`).

Result: **zero findings.** Every file contains real assertions against real behavior. Notable positives observed (recorded here for context, not as findings):

- `ArtifactPanel.live-preview.test.tsx` and `artifactComponents.test.tsx` pin iframe sandbox privileges (`allow-scripts` only, `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"`, injected CSP with `connect-src 'none'`) — security-positive, prevents privilege widening on refactor.

- `InlineWebSearchResults.test.tsx` asserts result clicks call `window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener')`.

Non-findings explicitly considered and rejected:

## Batch 301 — 20 files scanned

All 20 files in this batch are test files (`.test.ts` / `.test.tsx`). Each was read in full and checked against the taxonomy. The two findings below are test-quality issues (coverage illusion / test theater) where the test exercises a re-implemented copy of production logic instead of the real production code, so a real regression in the production path would not be caught.

### [MEDIUM] coverage illusion / test theater

- **File:** `services/api-gateway/__tests__/health.test.ts`
- **Line:** 11-20
- **Instance:** The health test builds a fresh in-test Express app via `createHealthTestApp()` whose handler is described as one that "mirrors the real implementation" — it never imports or mounts the actual api-gateway `/health` route handler.
- **Risk:** The real `/health` endpoint (auth middleware, dependency/readiness checks, status semantics) is never exercised, so the suite stays green even if the production health route breaks, regresses, or is removed — a false-green that gives misplaced deploy confidence on a gateway health check.
- **Fix:** Import and mount the real api-gateway app/router in the test (or hit the actual route export) instead of re-declaring a stub handler that mirrors it.

### [MEDIUM] coverage illusion / test drift

- **File:** `packages/unified-chat/src/stores/__tests__/chatStore.test.ts`
- **Line:** 396-415
- **Instance:** The persist v1→v2 migration test defines a local `loadMigrate()` that re-implements the migrate shape transformation inline (comment: "Re-implement the same shape transformation the store configures so the test stays decoupled from the persist plumbing") rather than importing and invoking the store's actual `migrate` function.
- **Risk:** The test asserts against a hand-copied duplicate of the migration logic, so a bug or drift in the real chatStore `migrate` (e.g. a renamed key the store forgets to map) would pass these tests while corrupting users' persisted conversations/messages on upgrade.
- **Fix:** Export the store's real `migrate` function and call it directly in the test so the production migration code path is the thing under test.

## Batch 302 — 20 files scanned

This batch is entirely the api-gateway test suite (19 vitest files + 1 setup file). Findings below are test-quality / drift issues; no production security flaws (the tests themselves are read-only fixtures and mocks). All hardcoded secrets encountered are explicit test-only fixtures (e.g. `setup.ts` `'test-jwt-secret-key-for-testing-only'`) and are the correct pattern, not findings.

### [MEDIUM] coverage illusion / copy-paste assertion duplicate

- **File:** `services/api-gateway/__tests__/routes/llm.test.ts`
- **Line:** 49
- **Instance:** The "excludes flagship models" test asserts `HOBBY_ALLOWED_MODELS.has('gpt-5.5')` is false on line 48 and then repeats the identical assertion on line 49, so one of the two checks is dead and no second flagship beyond `claude-opus-4.8`/`gpt-5.5` is actually verified.
- **Risk:** The wasted duplicate masks a missing assertion (a third flagship was clearly intended); a future regression that leaks another flagship into the Hobby allow-list would not be caught here.
- **Fix:** Replace the duplicated line 49 with the intended distinct flagship assertion (e.g. another Pro-only model id read from the catalog) or delete it.

### [MEDIUM] assertion theater / test proves nothing about production code

- **File:** `services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/worker.test.ts`
- **Line:** 532
- **Instance:** The `Step-up auth — insufficient_scope shape` test constructs a literal object inline (lines 534-538) and then asserts properties of that same literal; it never imports or invokes any production step-up/insufficient_scope code path.
- **Risk:** A coverage-illusion test that will stay green even if the real step-up response shape drifts or is removed, giving false confidence that the `insufficient_scope` contract is verified.
- **Fix:** Import and call the actual step-up handler/type-producing function (or remove the test) so the assertion is bound to production behavior.

### [LOW] test drift / hand-rolled duplicate of production app config

- **File:** `services/api-gateway/__tests__/integration/app.test.ts`
- **Line:** 46
- **Instance:** `createIntegrationTestApp()` hand-builds an Express app with helmet/cors/json middleware that is documented as mirroring production (lines 49-51) but does not import the real gateway app factory, so the "integration" tests validate a copy rather than the shipped config.
- **Risk:** Drift between the production middleware stack (CORS origins, helmet CSP, body limit) and this duplicate goes undetected — the headers/limit tests pass against the copy while the real app could differ.
- **Fix:** Import the production app/middleware factory under test, or add a structural assertion that the test app's middleware list matches the production one.

### [LOW] documentation drift — stale "scaffold only / skip path" comment

- **File:** `services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/providerStream.live.test.ts`
- **Line:** 13
- **Instance:** The header NOTE states "in this PR we only build the test scaffold (skip path) — fully exercising it requires standing up an Express app ... The skip path runs in CI clean", but the file below (lines 29-90) now fully stands up the Express app, stubs auth, and exercises the SSE path when `AGIWORKFORCE_LIVE_TEST=1`.
- **Risk:** Misleading comment makes a reader believe the live e2e is unimplemented, so they may not realize it actually performs real network calls with a real `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` when the env gate is set.
- **Fix:** Update the NOTE to reflect that the live path is implemented and gated on `AGIWORKFORCE_LIVE_TEST=1` + `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

### [LOW] redundant repeated dynamic import in a single test

- **File:** `services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/worker.test.ts`
- **Line:** 595
- **Instance:** The backward-compat test imports `../worker/index` three separate times (lines 595, 597, 599) to pull `registrationRouter`, `assignmentRouter`, and `heartbeatRouter` instead of destructuring all three from one import.
- **Risk:** Hygiene/debt only — three module-resolution round-trips and a brittle pattern; no functional impact.
- **Fix:** Destructure all three exports from a single `await import('../worker/index')`.

## Batch 311 — 21 files scanned

All 21 files in this batch are third-party Clerk SDK skill documentation (`.md`) under `.agents/skills/clerk-*`. Per the taxonomy, docs are scanned for documentation drift only, plus a structural scan for secrets/tokens/PII. No real secrets were found — every credential in these files is a documented placeholder (`pk_test_...`, `sk_test_...`, `YOUR_SECRET_KEY`, `YOUR_EXTENSION_ID`, `ticket_abc123`, `+12015551234`), which are illustrative, not live values. The findings below are documentation-drift / deprecated-API items in vendor docs.

### [LOW] deprecated API usage

- **File:** `.agents/skills/clerk-nextjs-patterns/references/caching-auth.md`
- **Line:** 9
- **Instance:** The caching example imports and uses `unstable_cache` from `next/cache`, which is deprecated in Next.js 16 (the version this monorepo targets) in favor of the `use cache` directive / Cache Components and `cacheTag`/`cacheLife`.
- **Risk:** Engineers following this skill doc in a Next.js 16 surface would add a deprecated, soon-to-be-removed caching primitive, creating future migration debt and inconsistency with the repo's Next.js 16 conventions.
- **Fix:** Update the doc to use the Next.js 16 `use cache` / Cache Components pattern (or note that `unstable_cache` is legacy/Core-2 only) with a per-user cache tag.

### [LOW] documentation drift

- **File:** `.agents/skills/clerk-nextjs-patterns/references/caching-auth.md`
- **Line:** 56
- **Instance:** The "Docs" link points to `nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/caching`, a path structure from the pre-Next.js-16 docs site that no longer matches the current Next.js caching guide URL.
- **Risk:** Readers clicking the link may hit a redirected or stale page describing an older caching model than the Next.js 16 the repo uses, reinforcing the deprecated pattern above.
- **Fix:** Point the link at the current Next.js Cache Components / `use cache` documentation.

### [LOW] documentation drift

- **File:** `.agents/skills/clerk-chrome-extension-patterns/references/headless-extension.md`
- **Line:** 55
- **Instance:** The headless-extension example wires a `chrome.tabs.onUpdated` listener that POSTs every visited `tab.url` to `https://api.yourapp.com/page-visit` on every page load, demonstrated without any user-consent gate, allow-list, or privacy note.
- **Risk:** An engineer copying this pattern into the AGI Chrome extension would exfiltrate the user's full browsing history to a remote endpoint, which conflicts with the product's local-first / privacy-by-default posture and would be a privacy-label/telemetry overreach if shipped.
- **Fix:** Add an explicit caveat in the doc that broad URL-reporting is a privacy-sensitive pattern requiring user consent and host/path scoping, and that LLM/decision logic stays on the desktop brain, not the extension.

### [LOW] documentation drift

- **File:** `.agents/skills/clerk-expo-patterns/references/push-notifications.md`
- **Line:** 24
- **Instance:** The push-token registration example writes the Expo push token to client-writable `unsafeMetadata` via `user.update()`, and the server send-helper (line 49) reads the token back from `unsafeMetadata` to address notifications, while the doc's own caveat (line 39) says verified/sensitive data should live in server-written `publicMetadata`.
- **Risk:** Following the primary example as-is stores a notification-routing token in a field any authenticated client can overwrite, enabling a user to spoof/redirect another field's trust assumptions; the doc presents the insecure path as the default and the secure path only as an aside.
- **Fix:** Make the doc's primary example use the Clerk Backend SDK to write the push token to `publicMetadata`, demoting the `unsafeMetadata` client-write path to a clearly-labeled non-production fallback.

### [LOW] documentation drift

- **File:** `.agents/skills/clerk-nextjs-patterns/references/server-vs-client.md`
- **Line:** 25
- **Instance:** The `'use client'` directive is shown as a parenthesized expression statement `('use client');` (also at line 81), which is a no-op string expression — not a valid module-top directive — if copy-pasted verbatim.
- **Risk:** A developer who copies the snippet gets a client component that silently behaves as a server component because the directive does not register, causing hooks like `useUser` to fail at runtime.
- **Fix:** Render the directive as a bare top-of-file `'use client';` statement without the wrapping parentheses.

### [LOW] documentation drift

- **File:** `.agents/skills/clerk-nextjs-patterns/SKILL.md`
- **Line:** 122
- **Instance:** The "Common Pitfalls" markdown table row for the API-matcher fix has an embedded literal pipe (`'/(api | trpc)(.\*)'`) that breaks the table cell boundaries, producing a malformed/garbled rendering of the matcher example.
- **Risk:** The matcher guidance renders incorrectly, so a reader cannot reliably copy the intended `'/(api|trpc)(.*)'` matcher and may mis-protect API routes.
- **Fix:** Escape the pipe inside the table cell (`\|`) or move the code example outside the table so the matcher string renders intact.

- **Instance:** The "Global Before Guard" example reads `userId.value` to gate navigation without first checking `isLoaded`, directly contradicting the file's own CRITICAL note at line 67 that `isLoaded` must be true before trusting auth state.
- **Risk:** A reader copying this example ships a route guard that can fire before Clerk initializes, redirecting authenticated users to `/sign-in` on first load (auth-redirect false-negative).
- **Fix:** Update the example to await Clerk readiness (e.g. gate on `isLoaded.value` / `clerk.loaded`) before evaluating `userId.value`, consistent with the file's own guidance.

### [LOW] documentation drift

- **File:** `.agents/skills/clerk-tanstack-patterns/references/router-guards.md`
- **Line:** 77
- **Instance:** The "Redirect After Sign-In" snippet uses `window.location.pathname` to build the redirect search param, but `beforeLoad` / loaders in TanStack Start run on the server during SSR where `window` is undefined.
- **Risk:** A reader copying this into a `beforeLoad` guard hits a `window is not defined` ReferenceError during server-side navigation, breaking the protected route.
- **Fix:** Source the current path from the router/route context (e.g. `location.href` from loader args) instead of the browser `window` global, or guard with a `typeof window !== 'undefined'` check.

### [LOW] documentation drift

- **File:** `.claude/agents/cli-engineer.md`
- **Line:** 38
- **Instance:** Smoke-test guidance hardcodes the expected CLI version (`agiworkforce --version` should print `1.0.0`) instead of reading the version from `apps/cli/Cargo.toml`.
- **Risk:** When the CLI version bumps, this agent prompt silently drifts and an engineer following it may "verify" against a stale version string and mis-report a passing/failing smoke test.
- **Fix:** Replace the hardcoded `1.0.0` with an instruction to read the current version from `apps/cli/Cargo.toml`, mirroring how the doc already tells engineers to read model IDs from `models.json`.

### [LOW] documentation drift

- **File:** `.claude/agents/chrome-ext-engineer.md`
- **Line:** 3
- **Instance:** The description hardcodes the extension version (`Chrome MV3 v1.2.0`), suite count (`14 test suites`), and `min Chrome 132` rather than directing the agent to verify them from `apps/extension/package.json`/manifest, unlike the other surface-engineer docs which instruct verification.
- **Risk:** A version/manifest bump leaves the agent description stale, so dispatch context cites an outdated version and an inaccurate suite/Chrome-min figure.
- **Fix:** Soften these to "verify current version/test-suite count/min-Chrome from `apps/extension/package.json` and `manifest.json`" consistent with the cli/mobile/vscode engineer docs.

### [LOW] stale state

- **File:** `.claude/local-archive/2026-06-05-doc-reset/ralph-loop.local.md`
- **Line:** 2
- **Instance:** Frontmatter declares `active: true` (iteration 74) for a ralph-loop session even though the file lives under `local-archive/2026-06-05-doc-reset/`, i.e. it was archived/retired.
- **Risk:** Any tooling that scans for `active: true` loop markers could re-treat a long-dead session as live; at minimum the flag misrepresents loop state to a reader.
- **Fix:** Set `active: false` (or remove the marker) when archiving a ralph-loop file so archived state and the `active` flag agree.

### [LOW] documentation drift

- **File:** `.claude/local-archive/2026-06-05-doc-reset/projects/-Users-siddhartha-Desktop-agiworkforce/memory/audit-2026-05-06.md`
- **Line:** 25
- **Instance:** The archived audit asserts "Surfaces that are production-ready: Web, ... all provider adapters" on the same page that lists an open P1 — "56 web API routes use service-role key directly (bypass RLS)" (line 16) — an unresolved trust/authorization gap that contradicts the production-ready claim.
- **Risk:** A reader skimming this historical archive could take the "Web ... production-ready" line at face value and overlook the still-open RLS-bypass backlog item, under-rating a real authorization-boundary risk recorded just above it.
- **Fix:** This is a historical archive (do not edit for accuracy); if any of this triage is still open it should be tracked in the current `docs/agent-context/known-flaws.md`, not relied on from this stale file. The live RLS-bypass item belongs in the active backlog if not already remediated.

- **Risk:** A user following the manual install path verbatim gets a silently-failing native messaging connection with no clear cause.
- **Fix:** Replace the placeholder with an obviously-templated token (e.g. `<EXTENSION_ID>`) consistent with the `<EXTENSION_ID>` placeholder used elsewhere in the same doc.

### [LOW] documentation drift

- **File:** `apps/mobile/README.md`
- **Line:** 48, 139
- **Instance:** Line 48 states the canonical iOS project output lives at root `ios/` and instructs "Do not create or hand-maintain a second tracked `apps/mobile/ios/` tree," but lines 139 references `apps/mobile/ios/` as an operational path used by `ios:device:dev:no-prebuild` ("only after the generated `apps/mobile/ios/` project is already in the right entitlement state"), and a `apps/mobile/ios/Pods/` tree is in fact present on disk (this batch's first 9 files).
- **Risk:** A contributor reading line 48 may delete/ignore the `apps/mobile/ios/` prebuild artifacts that the device-debug workflow on line 139 depends on, or be confused about which iOS tree is authoritative.
- **Fix:** Reconcile the two references — clarify that `apps/mobile/ios/` is an ignored (untracked) generated prebuild tree used only for device debug, while root `ios/` is the tracked Xcode-consumed project.

### [LOW] documentation drift

- **File:** `apps/mobile/scripts/release/EAS_SIGNING_RUNBOOK.md`
- **Line:** 60-73
- **Instance:** This file carries a "TODO for remaining surfaces" theming migration list, but `apps/mobile/scripts/release/README.md` line 354 declares this runbook "Legacy ... Superseded by this file" while saying the theming TODOs "stay in that file until the theming work lands," leaving an unmigrated/legacy doc with stale screen lists (`app/(app)/usage.tsx`, etc.) that can diverge from the actual codebase.
- **Risk:** The stale TODO screen inventory drifts from reality as theming work proceeds, misleading anyone who treats this superseded runbook as current guidance.
- **Fix:** Move the theming TODO into a tracked task or the canonical surface doc and mark this legacy runbook clearly as superseded at the top, or delete it once theming lands.

### [LOW] documentation drift

- **File:** `apps/mobile/scripts/wave0-smoke/README.md`
- **Line:** 230
- **Instance:** The failure-triage table documents that "In v1 (Wave 0), the download is a simulated timer" for the model-download step — i.e. the on-device model download is a stub timer, not a real download, while the surrounding runbook (Steps 5, lines 118-129) presents it as downloading a real ~2 GB Qwen3-4B model.
- **Risk:** A founder running the smoke test believes a real on-device model was downloaded and inference validated end-to-end, when the download is simulated; a genuine download/inference regression could pass this "GO" gate undetected.
- **Fix:** Make the simulated-vs-real download status explicit in Step 5 itself (not only buried in the triage table), and gate "Wave 0 GO" on the real download path once it lands.

### [LOW] documentation drift

- **File:** `apps/mobile/scripts/release/README.md`
- **Line:** 31, 43, 47-48
- **Instance:** Pinned tool versions are stated inconsistently across the runbook: line 31 says "pnpm 9.15.3 (matches repo `engines`)", line 43 pins "Node 22.12.0 + pnpm 9.15.3", while the mobile README stack table and `app.config.js`-driven flows elsewhere reference Node 22.x generically; these hard-pinned numbers are documentation that can silently drift from `eas.json`/`package.json` engines.
- **Risk:** If `engines`/`eas.json` bump Node or pnpm, these doc-embedded pins become stale and mislead release operators into installing the wrong toolchain version.
- **Fix:** Reference the single source of truth (`package.json` `engines` / `eas.json` base profile) instead of duplicating exact version numbers in prose.

Note (no finding): No hardcoded secrets, tokens, or PII were found. The Apple Team ID `D2PR62RLT4` is a non-secret public team identifier, and the founder email is a documented owner contact, not a leaked credential. No" yet on line 180 answers "Is all of the user data collected encrypted in transit? Yes" — if no data is collected, the encryption question should be Not Applicable, not Yes (and `android/data-safety.md` line 30 also answers Yes "for Cloud Managed paths", revealing the inconsistency).
- **Risk:** Internally inconsistent Data Safety answers (collect=No but transit-encryption=Yes) flag the form as contradictory during Play review.

## Batch 333 — 20 files scanned

This batch is composed entirely of Markdown documentation (audit ledgers, README files, BUILD/CONTRIBUTING/CHANGELOG/CLAUDE root docs), one Playwright accessibility-tree snapshot (`.md` AX dump), and one apply-patch test fixture (`bar.md`). Per the taxonomy, `.md` files are scanned for documentation drift only, and the large historical CHANGELOG was read in full (1675 lines, paginated) plus structurally scanned for secrets/tokens/PII. No secrets, credentials, API keys, or PII were found in any file; the only sensitive-looking identifier is an Apple Team ID (`D2PR62RLT4`), which is a public distribution identifier (it ships inside notarized app bundles), not a secret.

### [LOW] documentation drift

- **File:** `BUILD.md`
- **Line:** 78
- **Instance:** BUILD.md states desktop production bundles land in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/`, while the active desktop audit docs in this same batch (`audit/desktop-ui-computer-use/README.md` line 21, `audit/DESKTOP_UI_COMPUTER_USE_AUDIT.md` line 4) reference the workspace-root path `target/release/bundle/macos/...`.
- **Risk:** A new engineer following BUILD.md may look in the wrong target directory for the produced bundle/DMG, since the repo uses a shared Cargo workspace target dir; the two documented locations diverge.
- **Fix:** Reconcile BUILD.md to the actual emitted path (verify whether the Tauri config sets a crate-local or workspace-root target dir) and use one canonical bundle path across BUILD.md and the desktop audit docs.

### [LOW] documentation drift

- **File:** `audit/desktop-ui-computer-use/README.md`
- **Line:** 21
- **Instance:** The build-log row records the produced bundle as `AGI.app` / `AGI_1.2.0_aarch64.dmg`, while the sibling audit `audit/DESKTOP_UI_COMPUTER_USE_AUDIT.md` line 4 and several rows describe the bundle as `AGI Workforce.app`; the product-name doc convention (public brand "AGI", internal "agiworkforce") is applied inconsistently across the two evidence files.
- **Risk:** Reviewers tracing screenshot evidence to a specific app bundle cannot tell whether two different builds or one build under two names are being described, weakening the audit trail.
- **Fix:** Standardize the documented bundle name across both audit files to the actual `.app` product name emitted by the current Tauri config.

### [LOW] documentation drift

- **File:** `BUILD.md`
- **Line:** 41
- **Instance:** BUILD.md pins `cargo-audit` to version `0.22.1` in the optional-tooling install command; this is a hardcoded tool-version pin in a doc with no cross-reference to where CI pins the same tool, so it can silently drift from the CI-enforced version over time.
- **Risk:** Local `cargo audit` runs may use a different advisory-DB/tool behavior than CI, producing inconsistent vulnerability results between developer machines and the gate.
- **Fix:** Reference the single source that pins cargo-audit (e.g., the CI workflow or a tool-versions manifest) instead of hardcoding `0.22.1` separately in the doc, or add a note linking the two pins.

## Batch 337 — 20 files scanned

All 20 files in this batch are documentation (.md). Per taxonomy, docs are scanned for documentation drift (stale refs, broken contracts, claims about non-existent features, version/convention skew) plus structural secret/PII scan on machine-generated catalogs. Findings below.

### [CRITICAL] fake completion / implementation theater

- **File:** `docs/security/SECURITY-SUMMARY-2026-05-30.md`
- **Line:** 1
- **Instance:** The file named as the authoritative consolidated security summary is actually raw LLM scratch narration ("Good. The web supabase.ts doesn't exist... Let me create the comprehensive security summary now") followed by meta-commentary describing what the document _will_ contain ("the summary document will consolidate...", "The document preserves every still-open finding") — the promised consolidated finding doc was never written; the full 71-line file is the narration itself.
- **Risk:** Operators trusting this filename as the canonical security-finding ledger get a fake/empty deliverable; ~186 still-open findings (including the CHEXT-29 zero-click prompt-injection chain and JWT-in-localStorage) are referenced in unstructured prose with no per-finding evidence, so they can be silently lost when the source audit files are archived, leaving real critical vulnerabilities untracked.
- **Fix:** Either replace this file with a real structured consolidated summary (per-finding tables with file:line evidence and status) or delete it and point readers to the actual current security index, removing the misleading scratch narration.

### [HIGH] log leakage / excessive data exposure (live vuln IDs in repo-tracked doc)

- **File:** `docs/security/SECURITY-SUMMARY-2026-05-30.md`
- **Line:** 22
- **Instance:** The doc enumerates currently-still-open exploitable findings as a checklist (CHEXT-29 zero-click prompt injection + auto-execute, XCUT-01 localStorage JWT exfiltration, XCUT-02 "7 service files with SERVICE_ROLE_KEY time-bombs", MOB-02 unsigned Dispatch control messages, CLI-01 sandbox network policy fallthrough) in a repo-tracked file.
- **Risk:** A repo-tracked, unstructured roadmap of un-remediated critical vulnerabilities (with surface names and behavior) is a ready-made attack playbook if the repo leaks or before the items are fixed; it is also not actionable because it lacks file:line evidence to drive the fixes.
- **Fix:** Move open-vulnerability tracking into a controlled, access-restricted tracker with per-finding owners and file:line evidence, and keep only fixed/closed items in the public-tracked summary.

### [MEDIUM] documentation drift / stale catalog with hardcoded developer-machine paths

- **File:** `docs/reference/REFERENCE_INDEX.md`
- **Line:** 36
- **Instance:** (generated artifact — structural scan) This 1332-line reference image catalog self-declares stale (lines 7-9: "Some paths, counts, and labels may be stale after the 2026-06-06 cleanup") yet ships hardcoded absolute developer-machine paths like `/Users/siddhartha/Desktop/reference/...` across 640 entries; structural scan found no API keys/secrets (grep hits for "token"/"password" are descriptive text about screenshot contents, not credentials).
- **Risk:** Every consumer of this index outside the original machine gets broken paths and counts the doc itself admits may be wrong, so any claim derived from it (provider counts, surface counts) is unreliable and the catalog drifts further from reality each cleanup.
- **Fix:** Regenerate the index from a fresh on-disk inventory and store paths relative to a documented reference root, or mark the file archived and exclude it from current-doc consumption.

### [LOW] PII leakage (owner name embedded in repo-tracked reference descriptions)

- **File:** `docs/reference/REFERENCE_INDEX.md`
- **Line:** 256
- **Instance:** (generated artifact — structural scan) The personal name "Siddhartha Nagula" appears 649 times across image descriptions (e.g. hero-greeting "Good evening, Siddhartha Nagula") in this repo-tracked doc.
- **Risk:** Real-name PII baked into a doc that may be published or shared broadens the owner's exposure surface and embeds personal data in version control with no redaction path.
- **Fix:** Redact the personal name to a placeholder (e.g. "[user]") when regenerating the reference index.

### [LOW] documentation drift / missing required status headers

- **File:** `docs/security/auth-role-service-role-body-checks.md`
- **Line:** 3
- **Instance:** This current decision doc has only `**Status:**` and omits the repo-required `Owner` and `Last updated` headers that `docs/README.md` line 54 mandates for current docs.
- **Risk:** The doc fails the repo's own docs-status contract, so ownership and freshness can't be verified and `pnpm docs:check`/status-header checks may flag or skip it.
- **Fix:** Add `Owner:` and `Last updated:` header lines to match the required current-doc header block.
